The unfortunate goal of education is degraded by the state to attendance at state institutions, which are characterized by lack of freedom, forcing obedience and conformity. The contribution will focus on specific examples and cases concerning the rights of children and parents in education, for example: Does a child lose the right to personal contact with a parent by entering school? Can the school ban children from using cell phones and making recordings? Where is the line between a teacher's strict approach and humiliating and bullying a child? How can children and parents defend themselves?

As a lawyer, even in her private life, Zuzana promotes the freedom and responsibility of each individual for himself and his family, less state interference in human lives and respect for the individuality of each individual. She also works in the Human Rights League as an independent lawyer. It focuses on the legal defense of individuals, especially children, parents and patients, against interventions by institutions and the state, currently especially against unreasonable measures in connection with covid. She founded the advisory Facebook group Rights of children and parents in contact with healthcare, education and the state.

Four reasons for separating education from the state!
Education is monopolized by the state. He also decides on the conditions for the establishment and operation of private schools. Educating children in a way not approved by the Ministry is not legal even if it is the world's long-term successful learning methods. Parents with a different view on education are threatened with having their children taken away and imprisoned.
Like any monopoly, the state also provides expensive and low-quality services in education. Tabled teacher salaries discourage the able and attract the less able. The education provided by the state does not reflect the real needs of children - many important things are missing and a lot of unnecessary things remain. 
Even before reading, writing and arithmetic, a child learns to obey the authority assigned to him at school. It is difficult for him to start establishing equal relationships when he spends the entire educational process in a subordinate role. The logical consequence is a society full of conforming individuals always ready to submit to dictates and pressure from the outside.
Centralized education is used by states to indoctrinate young children. Each generation learns from a young age about the advantages of the regime it lives in and the disadvantages of other regimes. This effectively prevents critical thinking and constructive debate about the social order.

Four reasons why the state should not protect us!
Whenever the state protects us from any danger, it assumes part of the responsibility for our life. In that area, we have less freedom, which politicians take away from us through laws. The more "protected" we are, the less we make decisions about our lives.
The less we make decisions about our lives and the more the state protects us, the less we are able to take care of ourselves. Instead of ourselves, we rely on laws, politicians, government and government assistance. We are trying to solve a new problem with a new claim on the state. We are becoming dependent on the state.
The more people depend on the state, the more likely we will pass this dependence on to our children and future generations. Instead of self-confident and responsible individuals, society will be made up of people who are "entitled" to state aid.
If society is made up of people who "entitle" to state aid, it will cause a spiral of constant state growth. We will be "protected" even where we don't need or want it. Under the guise of protecting us, politicians will abuse their power and impose their ideas on how we should live.

--------
Four reasons to remember opportunity cost!
We live in a world of limited resources. So anything we do carries with it what is called an opportunity cost—that is, whatever we gave up in favor of what we did. It cost us at least time, but often something extra.
If we go to the movies instead of the gym, we sacrifice the opportunity to improve our fitness for the opportunity to watch a movie. And in exactly the same way, even nobler goals - for example, protecting the environment - are always realized at the expense of something - for example, treating the sick.
Every law, every regulation, every regulation, every investment, simply any state intervention has a price – not only money paid in taxes, but also unproduced goods, unprovided services, unrealized projects, jobs that will not be created, our time and the possibility of choice.
Opportunity costs must always be taken into account, i.e. when evaluating any state agenda - new or existing. The benefit of people spending their own money according to their preferences cannot be replaced by any state agenda.

Four Reasons Why We Need Market Prices!
Prices are a brilliant and irreplaceable tool to convey information. If something is in short supply, the price rises, which informs and motivates all market participants. The one who directs resources to the production of scarce goods or invents a substitute for them will earn. In the event of a surplus, the price falls again and resources are shifted elsewhere.
Prices also determine consumer behavior. Higher prices motivate consumers to save on scarce goods, or to replace them with something else - cheaper and therefore less rare. This saves not only human labor but also natural resources.
We influence the money in the market what we are really interested in. This leads to a better allocation of resources than when the state decides based on the will of the voters. Through elections, everyone tries to assert their abstract preferences at the expense of others, and thus projects are created that people would not spend their own money on.
In a truly free and free market undistorted by the state, those who can best satisfy the needs of the people who willingly pay for it will become the richest. Not those who are fine with politicians and officials making decisions about other people's money.

Four Reasons Why Democracy Is Not As Good As They Tell You!
Even a democratic majority can be wrong. In addition, he decides on things that everyone can decide in his own way. We don't need a one-size-fits-all solution. You make the best decisions about your affairs and money yourself, because you know your needs better than others.
Under the communists, the leading role of the Communist Party was enshrined in the constitution, today we have compulsory democracy. However, democracy without questioning and without restrictions can easily become totalitarianism, i.e. a system affecting all areas of people's lives. There are more and more things that we would like differently than they are democratically decided.
Democracy breaks up society because it turns people into rivals. If we could live our own lives, we wouldn't have to mind people with different values. However, when they can impose their views on us through elections, they are dangerous for us. Instead of tolerance and cooperation, we compete for a share of the collected money; about what we can and can't do.
We are not prospering as we could because of democracy. For more and more people, using the neighbor's state for part of their earnings is more attractive than working as hard as they do.  Therefore, there are more and more "entitled" ones, while those who create values are decreasing.

Does it make sense to store value in Bitcoin? How can we be sure that we will not lose our savings? Nowhere at all; we never have such certainty, because it simply does not exist. While cryptocurrencies are the money of the future, they serve as better stores of value than fiat currencies; however, no one can guarantee that it will not crash unexpectedly.
However, who can guarantee such a thing with fiat? Also no one; however, it is surprising how certain a number of people consider them to be. At the same time, the lifespan of an average fiat currency does not even exceed the productive life of an individual; it's just hard to save for retirement in them. So where does the unfounded confidence come from? Well, where there is a lack of data, there is room for state propaganda.

One of the regular listeners – Petr Firefanatic Hála – disagreed with my concept of marginal utility theory on one of the streams; he did what I hope others of you will follow: He debated me on the record on the subject; and it gave rise to an interesting debate about the economy, which can hopefully bring something to others as well. Although many people already understand why socialism and central planning in general do not work, there is a belief in society that certain industries must be centrally planned by the state because "it cannot be done otherwise"; and healthcare is unfortunately one of them. People are afraid that under capitalist health care, "the poor would die in the streets", which they are trying to fix with socialist health care; in that, unfortunately, people die as a result of misallocation of resources, but it's not seen as much because no one says to anyone, "We're not providing care." But it happens in practice, or the care provided is completely inadequate; as a result, of course, a lot of people die, although it is impossible to measure exactly how many there are, but sometimes specific cases can be pointed to.
As a doctor, Tereza has first-hand access to that system; in this livestream you can ask her anything you can think of on the topic. You can also call our Studio via Skype!

Although most people imagine something under the term "monopoly" - and even suspect that it is something harmful; however, few distinguish between a true monopoly and a dominant market player, but what's worse - the biggest, most harmful, most violent and most widespread monopoly is completely neglected and ignored. Yes, this is a state that can afford everything that no one else could afford. How is that? Well, by consistently abusing its monopoly position in education, it constantly indoctrinates everyone with its propaganda from the earliest age; people are then willing to view the state in a completely different way than all other subjects.
Through the analysis of the monopoly position of the state, the attitudes of anarcho-capitalists can also be clearly described. Contrary to popular belief, they do not want a world without the services that states provide; in fact, they only seek to de-monopolize the state and enable competition.

What if someone had a child dying in anarcho-capitalism that would require 50 million to save, which they didn't have? What then? How would the market deal with this!? Well, the state probably wouldn't ask for another 5 million in protection money (called VAT) from the money that people voluntarily collected. And what if someone was dying in capitalist healthcare because there was no money to treat them? Well, in that case at least he would know and maybe have a chance to try to do something about it; it happens all the time in socialist healthcare, it's just not talked about and no one calls the cases that way. And what is the price of human life? Can something like this be converted into money at all? Don't anarcho-capitalists do something like that? Well... SÚKL definitely does.

The Czech libertarian movement is one of the strongest in the world; and although most viewers of this channel know its current active personalities, not everyone knows the "previous generation" that laid the foundations of this movement. One of the most important giants of the Czech libertarian scene is Professor Josef Šíma. There are a number of barriers and pitfalls in communication with socialists and generally everyone from the opposite side of the opinion spectrum; however, many of them are more communicative in nature than fundamental. In the second half of the video, we discussed the universality of argumentation; or rather its absence - and the resulting very "popular" argumentative fallacy, which I demonstrated on the examples of the prohibition of incest, the decriminalization of drugs, the voluntary nature of vaccination or the obligation to fasten seat belts in the car - simply on the "tastes" themselves.

– Urza (www.urza.cz); author of Anarchocapitalism; creator of Freeport; co-founder and head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of the Freedom of Learning board

In the video, we explain why basic income does not work not only from the point of view of economics and mathematics, but above all, what would be its harmful effects on society even if it were to work by some miracle. Sure, in theory, a basic unconditional income could reduce red tape and simplify the benefits system; but at what cost?

The four types of market failures (imperfect competition, information asymmetry, public goods and externalities) are taught in every possible economic school, constantly repeated and taken more or less as a given; unfortunately, they are not discussed much anymore, and in addition, many people do not even think about them much, they simply learn them for the test and continue to take them as fact. I certainly do not want to contradict what economists are so fond of proving, namely that market allocation is not Pareto-optimal; however, I would like to discuss what it even means and what consequences can be derived from it (and especially point out what consequences cannot be derived from it, although unfortunately this often happens). And does it even make sense to call something like this a market failure?

Adam Růžička's lecture for the "Free Harbor Conference 2020: Totality yesterday, today and tomorrow" was entitled "Creeping social tyranny and the importance of freedom of speech".

Under the term tyranny, we usually imagine the violent dictate of a powerful individual or group that oppresses the rest. However, thinkers have long pointed out that tyranny can also manifest itself on a social level, in ways that are harder to define, but all the more insidious, because they are not clearly visible, but often have a comparable influence on the lives of individuals as despotic governments. This threat to free societies was described by John Stuart Mill in his famous essay On Freedom, and Václav Havel also touched on it in The Power of the Powerless when he spoke of social "self-totality". The lecture will present the basic theses of the issue of social freedom and connect them with recent psychological research in the context of the current challenges of democratic societies (e.g. social media, opinion bubbles, the phenomenon of divided societies, etc.).

After studying psychology at Masaryk University, Adam Růžička, MSc. MRes. at University College London, where he worked for several years as a researcher in the field of cognitive neuroscience and researched the brain with a focus on human speech. He currently works as the director of the H21 Institute in Prague, which focuses on collective decision-making, electoral systems, civic participation and the issue of a divided society.

The next speaker at the "Freeport Conference 2020: Totality yesterday, today and tomorrow" was Jan Zugar with his lecture "North Korea - a country much more open than we perceive it".

There is perhaps no country more emotionally closed to the outside world than the Democratic People's Republic of Korea. In 1950-53, a war took place here, during which the country was divided into southern and northern parts due to the efforts of the north, which sought, with the support of China and the Soviet Union, to unite the entire country under the red flag. This failed thanks to the intervention of UN troops, and so after a three-year conflict, Korea was divided into these two parts by the 38th parallel. While South Korea is a developing country that is moving in the same direction as comparable eastern states, North Korea is closed, an information embargo is imposed on the media of the surrounding countries, access to the Internet, which is also internal only to the DPRK, is almost impossible and the harsh dictatorship of the Communist Party and the Kim clan rules here. It is very rare to get to this country as part of diplomatic trips or a study stay, which Jan Zugar was able to do.

Jan Zugar is a graduate of BUT in Brno, a member of the Young Christian Democrats and an opponent of communism.

Any historian will tell you how historical totalities worked. But how to recognize future totalitarian ideologies and how to survive them? What is the fundamental difference between totalitarianism and dictatorship? Can totality arise only through the state, or are there real "grassroots" totalities from secret groups of fanatics?
In the study of totalitarianism, he gradually went from the historical to the systemic, political, sociological and psychological point of view, and the result is a synthesis of universally applicable principles of functioning of totalitarianism.

The second speaker of the "2020 Freeport Conference: Totality Yesterday, Today and Tomorrow" was Urza with his lecture "The Different Faces of Evil or Recognize Totality".

Although everyone can probably agree that they don't want to live in totalitarianism, for some reason totalitarian regimes are an inherent part of our history; and not only long past, but also quite recent, in short, they keep coming again and again. How is this possible, you ask, when almost everyone rejects totalitarianism? Well, few people offer it to people directly; totalitarian regimes typically come under the guise of promises of safety, prosperity, well-being, and often even freedom. Unfortunately, history shows that most people do not recognize totalitarianism until it is too late. And because Urza does not want (perhaps not only) to repeat this history, during this lecture he will try to teach you to recognize the arrival of totalitarian regimes while there is still time.

Urza is an anarcho-capitalist author; wrote about a thousand libertarian texts on the web and in print media and the first Czech book on anarcho-capitalism. For more than ten years, he not only reads, thinks and writes about freedom, ethics, the free market, the economy and the role of the state in society, but also lectures, makes videos and is invited to various programs and panel discussions. Together with his wife Teresa, he forms the Free Harbor; he heads the Czech and Slovak Institute of Ludwig von Mises, of which he is a co-founder; belongs to the board of the Freedom of Learning association and actively cooperates with many libertarian initiatives. title_en: Debate for puppets in the DISK theater
text_en:
The DISK Theater organizes a cycle of discussions "Debates for Puppets". This is footage from the first pilot test piece; the entire format is a constant work in progress, so future debates may look different.
The point of the discussion was that each participant was represented by a puppet as an avatar and did not know the identity of the others. I've been through a lot of debates; it's part of my job. This one was probably the most different from all the others; it was a nice change. I liked the idea at first glance, but only during the discussion did I fully appreciate it - one can focus much better on the topic itself and is not distracted by anything.
After the first part, from which the recording comes, there was a second one - with exposed faces; Unfortunately, the theater did not provide me with her recording. Anyway, I was surprised that a number of people in the audience recognized me (the best comment was: "I hope everyone knows an anarcho-capitalist when they hear one." - something that certainly wouldn't have been heard a few years ago); and the puppet debate probably served its purpose also in the sense that one of the listeners told me that for the first time she really listened to me without pre-judging me based on who I was (and she said what I was saying made sense to her).

– Urza (www.urza.cz); author of Anarchocapitalism; creator of Freeport; co-founder and head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of the Freedom of Learning board

title_en: Symposion 2019 at the Jan Kepler Gymnasium
text_en:
From an early age, each person consciously and unconsciously creates various bonds of various kinds with the environment; it is impossible to prevent something like that, it would probably not even be desirable. In general, we believe that everyone should have the freedom to make decisions about the ties in their life over time. Few people like organizations or sects that try to create strong emotional bonds in young children to be devoted to them before they are capable of effective critical thinking. The interesting thing is that they themselves see that the state is failing here, but instead of accepting it, they call for a state solution. Statism is pervasive and unfortunately affects even skeptics; and to some extent actually anarchists.

One planned lecture at the (de)Centrála club became a regular cycle (every first Wednesday of the month) due to great interest; the latter to some extent follows the cycle Anarchocapitalismus in Parallel Polis, although the format changes a little. I would like to shorten my talk, increase the space for discussion and deformalize everything a bit; moreover, I probably won't be the only one lecturing.
The topic of both the lecture and the discussion will be something that, in connection with the growing popularity of anarcho-capitalism, is increasingly coming under fire, namely monopolization in the free market. Will monopolies and cartel agreements arise without state supervision and antitrust authorities? How does the Austrian school of economics view monopoly? What about mainstream economics? Without a state, do we have anything to fear? If you are interested in answers - not only to these questions - do not hesitate to come!

title_en: Anarcho-Capitalism, Part Nineteen: In the Broader Context...
text_en:
How to go from a huge omnivorous state to anarcho-capitalism? And where does the road definitely not lead? We will also talk about this at the last regular lecture of this cycle. Many of you have rightly noted that most of the lectures were "one-of-a-kind" in the sense of applying the same principle to various branches of human endeavor. I would like to clarify and formulate this principle in general terms; especially for those who didn't notice it. And finally, we will place anarcho-capitalism in some context of the other anarchist schools, of which there are many and about which you will certainly hear a lot more.
Lectures by Urza (www.urza.cz).
Presentation: https://prednasky.urza.cz/ankup/

My favorite YouTuber (and probably the only one I follow) Martin Rota invited me to the program Zvědátoři, which he has been doing for a long time with Patrik Kořenář; the topic was - how else but - anarcho-capitalism!
And I have to say, it was a great discussion for me; Martin Rota is a logician, he has great arguments and overall he is one of the best opponents. Plus, I think live is even better than online. So I hope you enjoy watching the video at least half as much as I enjoyed making it.

A surprisingly large number of students came to the lecture; although they had many lectures to choose from, there weren't enough chairs in the end, so they had to sit on the furniture. They asked great questions; I consider the whole debate to be very constructive. Above all, in the end it turned out that almost everyone learned something new!

title_en: Anarcho-Capitalism on the Front Line: Social Issues
text_en:
Radio Free Transmitter (Slobodný vysielač) deals, among other things, with anarcho-capitalism in the program In the first line; they approached me to be their regular guest, which I happily accepted.
In this piece, we addressed the devastating effects of the welfare state on our society; and how would we be without him?

– Urza (www.urza.cz); author of Anarchocapitalism; creator of Freeport; co-founder and head of the Ludwig von Mises Institute; member of the Freedom of Learning board

As difficult as the free market provision of justice and internal security is, defense against an external enemy and, by extension, international relations represent by far the greatest challenge for a stateless anarcho-capitalist society. Can free people without a state defend themselves against aggressive conquerors? And if not, what will happen in the conquered territory? How does the control of a conquered anarchist territory differ from the control of a conquered state? Can the common survive without the state? Minarchists do not believe this; anarcho-capitalists do. Don't miss a lecture with a discussion on this interesting topic.
Lectures by Urza (www.urza.cz).
Presentation: https://prednasky.urza.cz/ankup/

While last time we only dealt with disputes in which both parties more or less cooperate, this time we will talk about cases of criminals and desperadoes who violate property rights and actively try to avoid the administration of justice. How will the free market deal with them? Isn't the state really needed here? This lecture is one of the three most "advanced" of the series and is a bone of contention between the anarcho-capitalists and the minarchists; so don't miss it.

How could a free market without states ensure a functioning judiciary? Who would appoint a judge? And would it be possible to appeal against the judgment? Is there any way to prevent the courts from favoring rich and wealthy clients? I will try to answer these - and many other - questions during the lecture; but first of all we get to the most interesting part: What would the courts decide if there was no central authority with a monopoly on legislation? This lecture is one of the three most "advanced" of the series and is a bone of contention between the anarcho-capitalists and the minarchists; so don't miss it.
Lectures by Urza (www.urza.cz).
Presentation: https://prednasky.urza.cz/ankup/

Anarcho-capitalism is finally being talked about! We are overwhelmed with questions and comments, the topic has already reached Jakub Janda from European values. A lot of people who don't know anything about anarcho-capitalism are also commenting now, but that's only good; please stay with us, be patient and help us spread the ideas of freedom!

– Tereza Sladkovská (future Urzová xD), longtime editor and author of the Ludwig von Mises Institute, member of Students for Liberty
– Urza (www.urza.cz), creator of Sewers of the Free Port, co-founder of the Ludwig von Mises Institute, member of Freedom of Learning

Do we need states in order not to devastate nature and the environment? If our society is only "managed" by the free market, will we leave our descendants with more than just contaminated water, air and soil? Without the state, who would protect endangered animal species? And how to promote sustainable development without the state? To explain this interesting issue, I will make considerable use of the knowledge of the Austrian school of economics, which we discussed (mostly repeatedly) in previous lectures; I highly recommend refreshing them again.
Lectures by Urza (www.urza.cz).
Presentation: https://prednasky.urza.cz/ankup/

Left-wing anarchists are often revolutionaries; anarcho-capitalists typically do not. However, we are individualists, as a matter of principle we do not group together and we are united, among other things, by our reluctance to blindly obey authorities, so there are exceptions to each of our "typicals". On the one hand, this is great, but on the other hand, in this particular case, I consider it extremely important to say a few words about it...

– Urza (www.urza.cz)

Youtuber Standa invited me to his online streaming show; and it was definitely an interesting interview. We talked about anarcho-capitalism; in the end, the audience could also ask their questions. Unfortunately, we didn't have time to go too deep, but thousands of people saw it, which I'm really happy about.

– Urza (www.urza.cz)

When the word "free market health care" is mentioned, most people immediately think of exorbitant amounts of money for medical procedures that the common mortal simply cannot afford to pay, leaving him with no choice but to live in sickness; or even die. Without the government, how could we afford to pay for medical care? Who would supervise the quality? How to overcome the enormous information asymmetry between doctor and patient in the market? Isn't free market healthcare an antisocial and horrible system through which the powerful can squeeze the powerless and sick? You will learn the answers to these and many other questions when you come to the lecture; and you can ask your own questions in the subsequent discussion.
Lectures by Urza (www.urza.cz).

title_en: Anarcho-Capitalism, Volume Thirteen: The Labor Market
text_en:
Do you think that without the state and its regulations, employees would have no standing, so employers could screw them over? In that case, this lecture is just for you! We will show why a free and unregulated labor market would not only not harm employees, but would, on the contrary, improve their situation in many ways; because the state provides its "protection" to employees as a bit of a disservice. Seeing exactly how and why this is so is not at all difficult; just come to the lecture, where we will talk about child labor and many other interesting things, among other things.
Lectures by Urza (www.urza.cz).

title_en: Anarcho-Capitalism, Part Twelve: The Social System
text_en:
Without the state, not only would there be no social benefits and unemployment support, but above all there would be no pension system as we know it now. What would that mean? In a free market society, would the poor starve to death on the streets? What would old people do without the state? I am going to answer these and many other questions at the twelfth lecture from the Anarchocapitalism cycle; subsequently we can talk about these topics in a discussion.
Lectures by Urza (www.urza.cz).
Presentation: https://prednasky.urza.cz/ankup/

The OKO association asked Freedom of Learning (with a capital S) for a lecture on the topic of Freedom of Learning (with a small s). The parents of the schoolchildren, but even the representatives of the city, arrived at the lecture; the reactions were surprisingly positive.
Although it was already possible to arrange the sound in such a way that I could be understood well, unfortunately, the same cannot be said about the questions from the audience, for which I apologize. The presentation on the wall was glossy, so it couldn't be caught on camera; making videos is not as easy as it might seem.

– Urza for Freedom of Learning

Support the first Czech book on anarcho-capitalism:
http://kniha.urza.cz/

title_en: HCPP17: Liberate education from the state!
text_en:
Compulsory school attendance is not only immoral, but it also represents the initial reason for our economic lack of freedom; State education costs money, also it's a source of state propaganda and statist indoctrination. This is the main cause of the conviction of people that the free market fails in so many areas, so we need the state authority to replace it. Why don't they teach us anything about the impossibility of economic calculation in the central planning? How easily can the authority of a teacher be replaced by the state authorities? And how can we keep the freedom when we spend the most important years of our lives in the jail?
Sorry for my horrible English; it is not so good in general and moreover I felt physically quite bad this time.

Presenting: Zdeňka Staňková and Urza (www.urza.cz) of Freedom of Learning (www.svobodauceni.cz).

title_en: Prague Business Club: Who would build roads?
text_en:
I was asked by entrepreneurs from the Prague Business Club to give a private lecture on transport infrastructure in the free market; I gladly accepted the offer and adapted the presentation to this target group, although the topic of course overlaps to a large extent (not completely) with the eleventh volume of the series Anarcho-capitalism from Polis.
If you are a skeptic and a practitioner of everyday reality, the lecture may be a little too optimistic and "visionary" for your taste; in that case, I recommend watching the lecture of the same name from the series Anarchocapitalism instead. Either way, the direction of the questions in the discussion is very different in both cases.

– Urza (www.urza.cz)

title_en: The Fight for Democracy (Urza vs. Bob Kartous)
text_en: Freedom of Learning hosted an unmoderated discussion between Bob Kartous and Urza on the topic of democracy in the education system in Paralelní Polis. We wish you a pleasant listening, although the debate was a bit heated in places and went into details.

The state appears to be an indestructible entity that has been with us as far back as history, so that no reason can be seen why it should not endure forever; but a similar institution, of which one could assume exactly the same thing, was already there - and how do you think it turned out?

– Tereza Sladkovská (future Urzová xD), longtime editor and author of the Ludwig von Mises Institute, member of Students for Liberty
– Urza (www.urza.cz), creator of Sewers of the Free Port, co-founder of the Ludwig von Mises Institute, member of Freedom of Learning

I was honored to be invited to the Liberal Institute's Mises Academy, where I gave two lectures.
This is a record from the second of them - about anarcho-capitalism; the audience consisted of people interested in freedom and libertarianism, to which the lecture was tailored. A more detailed treatment of this topic aimed at a wider public can be found in the list of videos "Anarchocapitalism in Polis".

I was honored to be invited to the Liberal Institute's Mises Academy, where I gave two lectures.

You can find a lecture on a similar topic aimed at a wider public in the video list "Anarchocapitalism in Polis" under the title "Anarchocapitalism, part seven: Education".

In discussing this topic online and in person with a number of people, I realized that it would be a good idea to make a video explaining what scientific evidence actually means and the difference between it and a mere experiment that does not disprove a theory.

title_en: Lecture at the gymnasium in Holice
text_en:
The students of the gymnasium in Holice invited me to the day of personalities to give them a lecture about anarcho-capitalism, freedom (and Freedom) of learning, education and the state; I gladly accepted and came, although the date conflicted with an invitation to the same event of another gymnasium.
Not only students and teachers arrived for the lecture, but to my surprise some parents too; in the end, an interesting debate was sparked, with the result of which I am certainly satisfied, but judge that for yourself.
Unfortunately, this is only an audio recording recorded on the phone, there is no picture, and the sound quality does not exactly allow for the most luxurious listening, for which I apologize; however, I find it listenable.
– Urza (www.urza.cz)

Parallel Polis organized a discussion on the topic "Sharing economy" - a phenomenon of today's time, an idol and a scarecrow. In-demand services that defeat established companies and scare the state with their success among users. 
Urza was invited as a guest, Tereza selected interesting moments from the discussion and added her commentary.

– Tereza Sladkovská (future Urzová xD), longtime editor and author of the Ludwig von Mises Institute, member of Students for Liberty
– Urza (www.urza.cz), creator of Sewers of the Free Port, co-founder of the Ludwig von Mises Institute, member of Freedom of Learning

Innovation can take place - and has for millennia - based on the voluntariness of resourceful and enterprising people; such a state is more than desirable and thanks to it our society continues to flourish. In addition, we unfortunately have an unrelenting, ravenous and expansive state that takes resources from the people against their will under the threat of using violence against them; even as a result of his interventions, various innovations arise, but at what cost?
Lectures by Urza (www.urza.cz).

Parallel Polis organized a discussion on the topic "Anti-Smoking Law"; is the government supposed to "protect our health" or should no one be forced to conform the rules of their business to the orders of the powerful?
Urza was invited as a guest, Tereza selected interesting moments from the discussion and added her commentary.

title_en: Anarcho-Capitalism, Part Eleven: Who Would Build the Roads?
text_en:
"If we had no state, who would build the roads?" So goes the most common question in libertarian jokes and one of the first reactions of statists to the mention of a stateless society; I am going to answer this very question at the lecture. And not only that! We will also talk about road traffic rules; would these differ from road to road if each road had its own private owner? After the lecture, as always, there will be a (perhaps heated) discussion; I look forward to hearing from you, especially if you disagree with me!
Lectures by Urza (www.urza.cz).
Presentation: https://prednasky.urza.cz/ankup/

title_en: Anarcho-Capitalism, Part Ten: Public Space and Freedom of Speech
text_en:
In the tenth lecture from the Anarcho-Capitalism series, we will focus on public spaces and places "for all"; how could such spaces exist in a stateless society based on respect for property rights? Who would manage them, why and for what? Would all parks disappear in cities? Would we live in concrete jungles without a bit of greenery? In addition, we will talk about freedom of speech; how does it relate to the topic? We will show that very closely. As always, the lecture will be followed by a discussion; I hope you will oppose me!
Lectures by Urza (www.urza.cz).
Presentation: https://prednasky.urza.cz/ankup/

Today we are thinking about the election of the French president (and we certainly do not envy the French that choice), the last election of the Czech president and, above all, what is the point of having a president (anywhere)...

– Tereza Sladkovská (future Urzová xD), longtime editor and author of the Ludwig von Mises Institute, member of Students for Liberty
– Urza (www.urza.cz), creator of Sewers of the Free Port, co-founder of the Ludwig von Mises Institute, member of Freedom of Learning

We will also look back in history and focus on a time and place when and where guns were virtually unregulated; what were the consequences? As always, the lecture will end with a discussion, in which you will be able to ask anything and, ideally, even oppose me.

We will also discuss the war on drugs that has been raging for decades; what did it actually cost us and what are its results? As usual, the lecture will be followed by a discussion, in which I will gladly try to answer all the questions you ask me.

Presentation of Freedom to Learn at LibertyCon 2017.
The government is indoctrinating our kids with propaganda of statism and evil; the solution is the separation of state and education!

Presenting: Urza (www.urza.cz) and Zdeňka Staňková of Freedom of Learning (www.svobodauceni.cz).

I consider this lecture to be the most important of the entire series on Anarcho-Capitalism; we will talk about the state education system as a powerful tool used to massively spread state propaganda. We will reveal the roots and effects of how current education works. Of course, there will also be an insight into how (and why) education could (and should) take place in a free market; and this time we will not only dwell on why it would not be such a horror as most people assume, but we will also look at the origin of those assumptions themselves. As always, the lecture will be followed by a discussion where I will answer all your questions and objections. Be sure to come this time!
Lectures by Urza (www.urza.cz).
Presentation: https://prednasky.urza.cz/ankup/

We fear that the nature of the problem goes far beyond this case.

As always, the lecture will be followed by my much-loved discussion; come and bring your friends who you think might be interested in this controversial topic.

In addition to the creation of new art, we will also devote ourselves to the protection of already existing works of art and cultural monuments; can this also be provided on the market? title_en: Anarcho-capitalism, part two: The state is a bad servant but a bad master
text_en:
In the first lecture from the Anarcho-Capitalism cycle, we talked about why the state is immoral. Come to the second lecture to hear why the state is even more inefficient. Anarcho-capitalism stands on two main pillars – natural law and the Austrian school of economics, the foundations of which will be presented at the lecture. But don't expect a dry talk about economics, we'll show everything with examples from the real world - for example, why does a top soccer player earn more than a firefighter who saves lives?
Lectures by Urza (www.urza.cz).
Presentation: https://prednasky.urza.cz/ankup/

title_en: Run the state like a business?
text_en:
For some time we have been hearing everywhere that it would be desirable to run the state like a business; and Babiš is far from promoting it alone.
It sounds quite "right-wing" and sympathetic; what do we say to that? We are not excited; watch the video to find out why.

– Tereza Sladkovská (future Urzová xD), longtime editor and author of the Ludwig von Mises Institute, member of Students for Liberty
– Urza (www.urza.cz), creator of Sewers of the Free Port, co-founder of the Ludwig von Mises Institute, member of Freedom of Learning

title_en: Anarcho-Capitalism, Part One: The State Is Immoral
text_en:
Come and listen to the introductory lecture from the series Anarchocapitalism! We talk about state funding and taxes; we will criticize the concept of taxes and their collection from the point of view of ethics. We will think through the consequences of what is behind every regulation and every law; how can their violent enforcement by the police be morally justified? And finally, we will say something about state propaganda and indoctrination; reasons why the state can basically do whatever it wants.
Lectures by Urza (www.urza.cz).
Presentation: https://prednasky.urza.cz/ankup/

There are two of us. We love freedom. We love anarchy. We love capitalism. We love each other xD
We are talking about a free market stateless society; yes, we know how it looks, even we thought the idea was absurd at first...
However, try to give her a chance; you can always refuse it.
Motto: "Good people don't follow bad laws."

– Tereza Sladkovská (future Urzová xD), longtime editor and author of the Ludwig von Mises Institute, member of Students for Liberty
– Urza (www.urza.cz), creator of the SEWER OF THE FREE HARBOR, co-founder of the Ludwig von Mises Institute, soulmate of the Freedom of Learning

April 19 was Bicycle Day, April 20 was Weed Day, and April 21 was the birthday of my friend and student from Ježek, with whom we filmed another episode of #ne_disobedience; this time I was breaking not only laws suppressing external freedom, but also social norms limiting internal freedom. Recording would violate both YouTube and Odysee's terms of service, which (unlike state laws) I respect; you can find it here. Coming soon. And since I want to give it more (your) attention, there won't be any other content for a few days, so this one has more space.

title_en: I will finally perform at Chaincamp!
text_en:
Chaincamp organizers have been inviting me for several years; and it always coincided with something for me (and when it didn't, the Chaincamp date was moved to another, where it already coincided with me xD). Now I will finally perform! I'll be talking about #disobedience, freedom, self-control, but also love - and how it's all connected. In addition to the lecture, I will also be in one (improvised) dialogue; both on Saturday - you can find everything in the program at
conference website
.

title_en: Today's Movie with Discussion: The People vs. Larry Flynt
text_en:
Students for Liberty approached me with an idea for an event where we would screen films and then discuss them; although it didn't seem like it at first, we managed to find a cinema willing to show us The People vs. Larry Flynt - I loved that movie as a child, but over time I see more and more themes important to freedom in it. Over time, I also learned a lot of interesting things about the shooting itself; I'm more than happy to share them - as well as an explanation of why I think this particular film is so essential. You can have more
read here
; and if you were interested, more
buy tickets
a
arrive at 1930 in the evening
!

It starts today
school year
; and with it, unfortunately, another regular wave of coercion, euphemistically called
compulsory school attendance
. If any entity other than the state allowed itself to threaten to forcibly remove children from parents who decide to educate them differently than that entity orders, we would consider it completely unacceptable. Why then?
it feels right to the vast majority of people
, so that OSPOD takes children away from their parents only because they are educating them contrary to the ideas of the Ministry of Education and Culture, including in cases where
there is no abuse or neglect
? And what kind
educational models outside the scope of our legislation
do they even exist?
Because I consider free education to be the key to a free society, I started working in
A hedgehog without a cage
– in my opinion, the least unfree school in the Czech Republic; there I understood that even more dangerous than indoctrination by state propaganda is the obedience we teach children from an early age. A lecture is typically dedicated to children and education in September, however, this year I will be in Brno on the first Wednesday (but instead, I would like to publish a recording of the last lecture within two weeks
#disobedience
); on Thursday, however, you can look forward to
livestream of the Freeport Studios
about education with Anička Rous, who is now very active in free-spirited activities.

The holidays are over
Sewers
therefore, they resume their standard operation; and with Stokami the whole
Free port
.
At the same time, we ask all authors to send texts to Stok; and anyone about any
financial support
our other activities.
It awaits us in the following days
Prague
a
Brno
launch of the book Anarchoagorism, more joint events with SFL (eg
film screening
), my appearance on
Chaincamp
and an early release of the recording from the last one
#disobedience
.
Regular activities like
lectures
or
live streams
they also continue; and I'm really looking forward to seeing you again!

And then there are the holidays, which affect quite a few of us in some way, be it school children, their parents, university students, teachers, visitors to various festivals and the like; The readership and viewership of texts and videos of the Free Port decreases every year during this period. So I'm putting Freeport into vacation mode for two months, which means less content and less regularity; in the meantime, we will not only diligently prepare for the 2026/2027 season, rest, finish the rest, but after all, something will happen during the holidays (for example, a stay in the House of the Free Port).
At the same time, I am asking all Stok authors for more texts; and thanks in advance! Enjoy the summer everyone; and above all life!
Today at 11:30 I will perform at BTC Prague; I will talk about the power of peaceful dialogue.

You don't know what? Czech flag day! I consider statism to be the greatest and most dangerous world religion of the present and past; like most religions it has different churches (in the form of individual states); they have their sacred symbols (flags, insignia), places (palaces, monuments), texts (constitutional documents, founding declarations) and songs (marchs, hymns), holidays (celebrations of victory, formation), celebrations (parades, military parades), relics (standards, crown jewels), officials (politicians, officials), symbolic gestures (salutes, laying of wreaths), saints (honored by statesmen, national heroes) and ceremonies (elections, coronations). Many states celebrate their flags on various important days for them (coronations, deaths, battles, enactment of flags, etc.); in the Czech Republic it could be March 30, which is the day of approval of the 106-year-old Act 252/1920.
In 2020, it was proposed by the Czech Vexillological Society, which at the time interested few people; six years later, Babiš probably needed to act as a patriot, so he proposed it in the amendment to Act 245/2000. So do we have it? Czech flag day in the law? Nope. Not even a week before the big day, the senate returned it. That they wouldn't want to weed out the legislation with such nonsense? But somewhere! It is said that this would make the other six national symbols (large and small coat of arms, tricolor, standard, seal and anthem - from their
performance ended at the police station
I remember them off the top of my head); they prefer to rename the St. Wenceslas Day to the Day of Czech Statehood and State Symbols. The proposal will be taken up again by parliament... Hundreds of (well-paid) man-hours (of taxpayers' money) are spent telling us what day to fly the flag. How can anyone take this seriously?

title_en: Murray Newton Rothbard's One Hundredth Birthday
text_en:
Today, the "Father of Anarcho-Capitalism" Murray Newton Rothbard would have celebrated his hundredth birthday if he were alive; I see the greatest contribution of his work in the consistent and logical introduction to the consequences of two trends - which were seemingly not very related - anarchism (anarcho-individualism) and the Austrian school of economics. Early anarchists typically did not understand economics very well, while proponents of the Austrian school of economics did not apply their (otherwise correct) conclusions to the state; Murray Newton Rothbard corrected both and came to a brilliant conclusion: "Capitalism is the fullest expression of anarchism, and anarchism is the fullest expression of capitalism. Not only are they compatible, but you can't really have one without the other. True anarchism will be capitalism, and true capitalism will be anarchism." This knowledge and full understanding of it changed my life greatly; Thank you, Mr. Rothbard.
In honor of his 100th birthday, Free Harbor is hosting a Saturday
freedom conference
; it will feature eight speakers with quite different views - from democratic to anarchist (however from three quite different directions) to self-development and spiritual. I would like us to listen to their performances and treat them as the late Murray probably would have done; please, let's try to be open to them, not to judge them and to take from them what makes sense to us - perhaps this very conference will lay the foundations in one of us for something that no one has yet invented and that is still waiting for its discoverer, which could be you. We will try to ensure that all lectures are published in
Freeport Channel
; however, nothing can replace the atmosphere at the place. I look forward to seeing you!

What would you say to a person who would murder someone he doesn't even know and excuse it by saying he's not responsible because his boss told him to do it? That's probably a pretty absurd defense. But why do we accept it for soldiers in the army? I understand that in case they have to enlist, desertion is punishable by death, so they were compelled to do the same by force; but why remove the responsibility from the soldiers who signed up for it voluntarily? After all, it is only their risk to murder someone who has done nothing to anyone in the course of their profession; even a professional driver probably has a higher chance of killing someone than the average person, but we don't tolerate it either. Why should murder in war not be murder? Just because it
the state pressures the people with its propaganda
? Will you say that "there is no other way"? Then imagine how much better the world would be if people weren't taught that sometimes murder isn't murder when it suits the powers that be.

I recently listened to a (years old) recording of a kind of discussion with Petr Gazdík; in it he explained, based on his past and "life story and background", why he would never take a bribe. Let us suppose for a moment that he was telling the truth, and that he is seriously a proud incorruptible man; immediately afterwards, with considerable pride in his voice, he declared that the gambling lobby would never break him and that he would fight against gambling for the rest of his life, otherwise he would not be able to look in the mirror. That person is very likely not even aware that they are pushing
violent persecution of some group of people and trampling on their property rights
; and you know what's worse than a politician initiating aggression towards you? Well, much worse is a politician initiating aggression towards you who cannot even be bribed to stop it. Even if all those who "mean it well" sit in the parliament (and we are far from that), the state will not start working in our favor; on the contrary, sometimes it can be even worse.

To answer the question of whether I am infringing by damaging my reputation
property rights
(and thus I am attacking and the victim can defend himself with force), one must first determine whether the reputation can be owned. My reputation is actually people's opinions of me; reputation is what others think. And can I own the thoughts and opinions of others? Certainly not. So how could I own my reputation? It is not possible; it is not my property or decision what others will think of me. Therefore, when someone slanders me, it is appropriate to respond to it, refute the slander or ignore everything (it depends on the decision of each of us); however, it is not adequate to use physical violence and limit the freedom of speech and property rights of the slanderer, since he did not attack my property, since I do not own my reputation (that is, other people's opinions). He may have harmed me, but that in itself does not constitute a violation of property rights; if my partner leaves with him, it can also harm me, but it is not appropriate to solve the situation with violence.

On my beautiful journey through life, I meet many opponents of anarchism or capitalism, most often both. Anti-capitalists typically dislike greed, selfishness, that some have little and others have much, inequality... These phenomena are seriously present in capitalism; but its regulations do not disappear. Greedy selfish people go into the service of the state, where they continue to dig (depending on the regime, they may focus on power, acquaintances, etc. instead of money), only the selfishness is not used to satisfy the needs of customers; and although inequality can be reduced by state interventions, it is only in such a way that the well-being of society is significantly reduced, because inequalities arise from the growth of well-being - the market is not a zero-sum game (voluntary exchange increases the benefit of both parties); inequalities typically arise when someone improves the lives of a lot of people a little, while improving himself by leaps and bounds. Anti-capitalists criticize the things they don't like, but they miss the fact that these are not the consequences of capitalism, but features of the world that socialism declaratively changes, but in reality only transforms them into something much worse.

On my beautiful journey through life, I meet many opponents of anarchism or capitalism, most often both. Anti-anarchists typically resent the idea of a society without a central authority usurping a monopoly on violence. "Society cannot function without rules," they say; and they are right! But even the anarcho-capitalists do not care about the functioning of a society without any rules, they do not want to have those rules dictated from above by a central authority, but support their market emergence on a decentralized basis. Let everyone determine their own rules on their property, in their business; simply where he bears responsibility at the same time. And if several people collaborate on something, let them freely agree on the terms of collaboration; and if they don't suit them, they don't have to cooperate. If it becomes too complicated for people, there is nothing against it if they voluntarily start following uniform standards; but let those who do not wish such a thing be forced to do so, even if they were in the minority. Anarchy is not the absence of order; just the absence of a central authority.

We often hear the phrase "freedom and democracy"; in reality, "freedom or democracy" is more valid.
Democracy tends to be the nemesis of freedom
. What is democracy? High-flown talk aside, this is the tyrannical rule of the majority; yes, violent, because against people who do not obey the laws dictated by the majority,
the state routinely uses violence
. Will the majority decide to disarm the minority? It will happen. Will the majority decide to raise taxes on the minority? It will happen. Will the majority decide to limit free speech? It will happen. Will the majority decide that we must solve the Jewish question? It will happen. That current non-democratic regimes are typically far less free? Sure; however, this does not change the above - just as the existence of an extremely toxic green toadstool does not make a poisonous red toadstool an edible mushroom.

title_en: Thirty-one years since the death of Murray Newton Rothbard
text_en:
Today marks thirty-one years since the "Father of Anarcho-Capitalism" Murray Newton Rothbard left this world at the premature age of 69; his life's work was a consistent and logical introduction to the consequences of two trends - which were seemingly not very related - anarchism (anarcho-individualism) and the Austrian school of economics. Early anarchists typically did not understand economics, and the proponents of the Austrian school of economics did not apply their (otherwise correct) conclusions to the state; Murray Newton Rothbard corrected both and came to a brilliant conclusion: "Capitalism is the fullest expression of anarchism, and anarchism is the fullest expression of capitalism. Not only are they compatible, but you can't really have one without the other. True anarchism will be capitalism, and true capitalism will be anarchism." This knowledge and full understanding of it changed my life greatly; Thank you, Mr. Rothbard.
Murray Newton Rothbard was born on March 2, 1926; that means he would be 100 years old this year. In honor of this, the Freeport is hosting
the seventh conference
on the subject of freedom; and the first Saturday after his hundredth birthday.

title_en: What do you wish for at the turn of 2025 and 2026?
text_en:
I don't have any New Year's resolutions; if I want to change, I see no reason to wait for the turn of the year. Yet I have a wish; I would like to finish and publish the book, continue with #ne_obedience (and didn't sit down), Harbor, Hedgehog and relationships and connect a little more with my body, rest and live healthier - I'm working on everything, some things are getting better, some things are worse (with the body). It's All My Way to Freedom (and Love); I want to live in a freer society, but it is clear to me that I can only change it by changing myself.
What about you? What are your wishes? What do you want from yourself? What about others?

I recently heard a wonderful argument in a discussion: "The state is too weak to defend itself against oligarchies and corporate influence." Erm... that's a rather idiosyncratic interpretation. So what about that? How to "strengthen the state"? More officials, more money, more control, more laws? Why it doesn't make sense and it won't lead to anything,
I have already explained many times
; here, however, it is even internally contradictory to the person's faith. If they believe that the state is controlled by oligarchs and large corporations (which is certainly true to a large extent), then how can the "strengthening" of that state (controlled by oligarchs and corporations) take place so that it is no longer controlled? After all, those subjects will also intervene in the entire process; and there is no reason to suppose why they should have less influence here than anything else. Do we want to get rid of them? Then let's get rid of the state! It makes no sense to claim that they control the state, but at the same time call for its strengthening; it's like upgrading the enemy's weapons.

Before, families were pretty solid units; parents took care of their children, who they then relied on in their old age, which of course still happens today, but to a lesser extent. Why? Modern socialist states came up with theirs
social policy and pensions
; thereby reducing the motivation of families to maintain good relations. Does that sound cynical? Is it much more complicated? Relationships aren't just about money, are they? Love can't be bought? Yes, sure! That's all true. I am not saying that if parents and children were more economically dependent on each other, there would be a paradise on earth, I am far from it; it's just that the motivation of the parent to maintain good relations with the offspring is higher if the parent knows that he will be dependent on the offspring one day, and on the contrary, the motivation of the offspring to take care of his parent is lower when he knows that the state does it anyway - and especially when he knows that this is a fundamental role of the state, which is constantly emphasized to us (
since childhood
), in addition, the state in question still pays from taxes (which means it has less resources).

Without this help, it would be difficult to create actions from writing uncouth texts and shooting videos on a phone leaning against a mug
#disobedience
or the emerging professional freedom documentary; thank you, thank you from the bottom of my heart And for everyone who reads these lines, whatever they think of my work, I have this wish: Today (and every day) enjoy (not only) Christmas, have a good time, be happy; and finally without typos this year:
MURRAY CHRISTMAS!!

Today is exactly ten years to the day
opening of Stok Free Port
; in 2015 it was a website with several authors and traffic from a few thousand devices per month (today it has hundreds of authors, traffic from thousands of unique IP addresses every day and tens of thousands per month). I created this place for libertarians to throw their thoughts (shorter than, say, a pro
Mises.cz
) and discuss them; it was the first project
Free port
, which didn't even exist at the time (and later got its name according to Stok). I liked and often said then that life has more imagination than we carry in our dreams; and really – if someone told me o
Studio
, the whole
Channel
, lectures and
Conferences
,
Hedgehog
and other projects with the reach of hundreds of thousands of people, I wouldn't believe it. Nevertheless, it not only happens, but above all it constantly motivates me to create more; I'm working on another book, a documentary about victimless crimes and preparing a big anarcho-agorist show.
For all this, I am grateful to my loved ones, colleagues, hedgehogs, but also to all of you who are still here, consuming and sharing content, helping, commenting, reacting, giving feedback and last but not least
you finance
the cost of salaries (although we also have an amazing team of volunteers), rent, gas, equipment and other expenses, for which I thank you from the bottom of my heart; without you, all of this would only be a fraction. One of the most active libertarian communities lives in the Czech Republic; awareness of us (and of anarchy) is spreading and our numbers are growing (although we are still a minority - but damned more numerous in the last ten years). Let's continue to discover, create, have a peaceful dialogue together and strive for the best versions of ourselves; and let's not forget that freedom is not given, freedom is taken - so let's enjoy it to the fullest.

It starts today
school year
; and with it, unfortunately, another regular wave of coercion, euphemistically called
compulsory school attendance
. If any entity other than the state allowed itself to threaten to forcibly remove children from parents who decide to educate them differently than that entity orders, we would consider it completely unacceptable. Why then?
it feels right to the vast majority of people
, so that OSPOD takes children away from their parents only because they are educating them contrary to the ideas of the Ministry of Education and Culture, including in cases where
there is no abuse or neglect
?  And what kind

Today I will venture a little beyond the boundaries of libertarian ideas (with which this text is only very loosely related); I would like to deal with the concept of revenge, which is often perceived by people as an act of justice. I do not share this view (although I probably thought so at some point in the past, but I no longer remember exactly); revenge makes no sense at all to me, except as an effort to deter the perpetrator - or others - from harming a person. However, it is not entirely clear to me where the wishes come from, for example, that a dead murderer (perhaps a terrorist) end up "in hell" or "may his soul be damned" (let's leave aside who believes in what; although atheism is common in the Czech Republic, in the USA, for example, everyone believes in an afterlife); I wish salvation to Stalin and Hitler, may their souls rest in peace. Because why not? It will not harm and benefit anyone; why not wish bad people good things in cases where it does not harm anyone and has no (un)educational effect?

We all know from experience with socialism that the state is not able to provide even such banalities as toilet paper or menstrual pads - in short, things whose need can be easily estimated and calculated; the reasons are explained by the Austrian school of economics, but let's leave the theory aside for a moment. Almost no one disputes that when the state tries to provide consumer goods, it fails; unlike the market. But why do so many people, despite the state's inability to provide absolutely trivial needs, believe in its ability to provide things that are much more complicated (education, health, justice, security...)? Especially when they witness the state failing in this day and day; above all, we must not give the market a chance, because "it certainly wouldn't work" (although there is no indication of this). So why do people still believe it? Well, one thing the state doesn't do so badly -
propaganda indoctrination always worked for him; and it is not surprising that the target is small children

Sometimes I hear complaints about "modern consumerist over-technological society" and its separation from "nature" (as if we are not even part of it); they say it's bad that people live in cities, use technology and don't have contact with the wild. I don't quite understand this rant; I don't understand why anyone lives a self-critical life. Why does he complain about "society" instead of giving up technology himself and spending time in the countryside instead of the city? Well, there are not many achievements of modern times, such possibility of social enjoyment, so many job opportunities and the like; yes, that's all true - welcome to the "idyllic" life of our ancestors (or rather, a "taste" of it; in reality, it was worse)! I don't see the "disease" of today in the cities or the "separation of man from nature"; I think the "disease" of today is rather how often we want something, but we are not willing to pay the price, but we complain that others who don't need it live badly.

title_en: Do you have a program for the weekend? Come to the Freeport Conference 2025!
text_en:
At this year's Freeport Conference, you'll hear plenty of perspectives on the culture wars; from conservatism being the freedom that progressivism takes away from us, to the exact opposite, to the attitude that the culture wars take away our freedom in and of themselves. And many more... Make up your own mind - ideally
on Saturday at 9 a.m. at the Law Faculty of the UK
!

What will happen to slot machine or roulette addicts if the state (even more) taxes gambling? Let's start with what will definitely not happen - these people definitely do not calculate that with a higher tax burden it is not really worth playing it anymore, and they will not stop doing it. How do I know? Well, if they were capable of it, they would have calculated it and stopped playing, because it didn't pay off for them even before; they'll lose enough of the games they put in the boxes anyway - and because they're addicted, they'll play enough of those games. The amount of tax that the state imposes on gambling only determines in what proportion the money of the addicts is divided between the gambling operators and the goons from the government; it does nothing to help addicts. Taxing cigarettes or alcohol can really reduce consumption, because it makes a difference whether a smoker pays three or five thousand a month for his bad habit; however, a gambling addict will pay whatever he can for his habit (that's the point of the addiction), so the tax won't help.

For a very long time, postal services were something that various states claimed to have monopolies; and people universally believed that it was actually necessary - everyone necessarily "knew" that the free market "wouldn't work" (just as everyone "knows" today in many other fields). Today it is clear how things are; a state monopoly for the delivery of parcels is completely out of the question in the vast majority of countries. Abolishing the state post office is not something that has broad public support, but here and there someone can be found, and above all, counter-arguments have already shifted from the position "only the state has to do it" to "in most cases, the private sector is more efficient". It's great to see an industry where public opinion has shifted from "the state must have a monopoly" to "OK, let it have competition" to "somehow we could do without the state (although we don't want to yet)". So when do you think the cancellation (or rather complete privatization) of the Czech Post will take place? Will we live to see it? And when will Czech Television start ringing the bell?

title_en: Do the laws of the market apply?

text_en: Ridicule of Christians - and creationists in particular - is quite common in the atheist Czech Republic (and as a Christian - albeit one who believes in evolution - I sometimes laugh heartily at such jokes); such insinuations are sometimes thoughtful, sometimes less so, however how about the following comment: "Christians (Creationists) are completely out of their minds because they believe in Darwin whose theories don't make sense." Isn't that absurd? It is indeed; and maybe that's why I've never heard this phrase. But I heard another - no less absurd: "Austrian economics is completely out of the question, because it assumes perfect competition, perfect information and perfect people pursuing their economic interests." This is no less nonsense than the Darwin thing; the Austrian economic school not only does not use any "homo economicus under ideal conditions" models, it even criticizes them very harshly, which does not prevent many from pushing these things into the Austrian economy anyway.

What would people do without state subsidies for science and research? So, above all, they would have more of their own resources (money), which they could decide for themselves; then basically two cases can occur: Either the person who has the money left in his pocket and the state did not collect it, decides to use it to finance some research (either directly or indirectly through the purchase of the product of the company that conducts the research - for profit or for another reason), the state is not needed for this; or would the person in question decide to spend this money (or part of it) in any other way - but what does this mean? That according to his own standards, what he spent his money on (whatever it was) brings more benefit to the person in question than the research that the state wants to force him to finance would bring him more benefit. It can be argued that the person in question will not correctly foresee all the consequences, but no one can do that at all; and if someone feels that someone else is doing it wrong, let them teach him, but
do not force him
!

I participated in a debate about whether the state should force restaurant owners to provide diners with a list of allergens; defense
violent coercion
she relied on two arguments: The first was that "after all, no one will miss out if she writes down the allergens"; the second concerned saving the lives of severe allergy sufferers. If "no one is missing" was a valid argument for violating property rights, then for example thieves who robbed many people of only a few crowns (rounding "errors") did not actually do anything because "no one was left". And the rescue of allergy sufferers? Don't be laughed at! Those who have such a severe allergy that they are at risk of death from anaphylactic shock have to take much more care (find out about the food, ask the staff, eat in "proven" places); relying on listings that sellers paid off just because someone pushed them is nothing more than another fruit of the government's efforts to make us irresponsible ignoramuses, which can't end well.

title_en: Thirty years since the death of Murray Newton Rothbard
text_en:
Today marks thirty years since the "Father of Anarcho-Capitalism" Murray Newton Rothbard left this world at the premature age of 69; his life's work was a consistent and logical introduction to the consequences of two trends - which were seemingly not very related - anarchism (anarcho-individualism) and the Austrian school of economics. Early anarchists typically did not understand economics, and the proponents of the Austrian school of economics did not apply their (otherwise correct) conclusions to the state; Murray Newton Rothbard corrected both and came to a brilliant conclusion: "Capitalism is the fullest expression of anarchism, and anarchism is the fullest expression of capitalism. Not only are they compatible, but you can't really have one without the other. True anarchism will be capitalism, and true capitalism will be anarchism." This knowledge and full understanding of it changed my life greatly; Thank you, Mr. Rothbard.
Murray Newton Rothbard was born on March 2, 1926; that means he would be 100 years old next. I should like to project it to the next Freeport Conference; so far I am considering fairly general topics - freedom or anarcho-capitalism. Do you have any tips to inspire me? I am sending in the New Year and the New Year
the wish of a wise Redhead
: "Have fun!"

Here we have another Christmas Day; it - and all of Christmas - in my eyes symbolizes Christian spirituality, capitalist materialism, anarchist enjoyment of life and the divine music that I share every year. As always, we'll start
Freddie
! Carol of the Bells is one of my two favorite carols, plus it has a lot of versions, so I put a different one here every year -
this year such an epic one from Samuel Kim
; a version of the latter was also recently created by my platonic love
Lindsey Stirling
. Unfortunately, they don't do my favorite Glitch Mob carols; so at least
Warrior Concerto
. I've been listening a lot this year too
Illenium
or
Seven Lions
; and I want to share about
this atypical one (and my favorite) from Emperor
. And just like last year I will close Pink Floyd;
album The Dark Side of the Moon
I was accompanied by something special this year.
I wish all people - and not only for Christmas, but above all for
everyday life
of our lives - above all, love and freedom; two values – two principles – that I consider perhaps the most important of all. That is why I am constantly getting to know them, looking for them, researching them and trying to live in maximum harmony with them; though it's more of a process - a lifetime of amazing work. In addition, lately I have been finding that they are much more related than I thought even two years ago; I'm just beginning to gradually formulate their connection, so I expect you'll hear more about it from me in the coming year - much like this year about inner freedom, which I'm also constantly progressing in knowing, as you can see from the insights I share. So enjoy your Christmas, have a good time, have a good time; and finally without typos this year:
MURRAY CHRISTMAS!!

text_en:
Last time
a lecture on anarcho-capitalism at the (de)Centrála club
I devoted myself to inner and outer freedom; it was very important for me, so please watch the recording and make any comments.
Markéta Čermáková will perform today; the topic will be – as every September – education.

We look forward to seeing you tonight at 7 p.m
of the (de)Central club
