Claude Frédéric Bastiat already showed more than two hundred years ago that such an approach does not make sense, does not bring anything good and is only harmful; because customers always choose the services that suit them best in the market, so any state intervention that causes them to reconsider their choice means that instead of the best option, they were forced to settle for the second best. However, this quite obvious truth has been skilfully disguised by various socialists, so that no one really cares anymore; because it was replaced by annoying populist propaganda on the topic of protecting "ours" from "foreigners", regardless of the fact that in the end the customer... "ours" will pay for it anyway.

In Texas, someone had a bright idea...and lo and behold, suddenly people over the age of twenty-one are allowed to carry guns on college campuses; of course, a number of professors and other left-wing intellectuals, who predict bloodbaths and student massacres, railed against the law. This change is the second reasonable adjustment to the laws regulating firearms in Texas in recent times; you could talk about the first one
read in Stoky in June
. Now let's keep a close eye on the long-term trend of crime in this American state, how many people will die in college massacres in the coming years compared to the past, and what all these deregulations in the field of weapons will bring to the residents there; if it turns out (which I strongly believe) that the situation is improving, hopefully it will lead to further loosening of unnecessary - and not just gun - laws - not just in Texas.

Recently, the frequency of terrorist attacks in Europe has increased dramatically; most of them are quite undoubtedly Islamic radicals, and I find it ridiculous to suggest that their motivation has nothing to do with the religion they profess. Most recent terrorists are Muslims, the ratio of terrorists among Muslims is higher than among followers of any other faith, and of course we have no reliable way to distinguish someone who just privately believes in Allah and doesn't bother anyone with it, from someone who intends to use their faith as an excuse for sadistic murder; what about that
Before you answer this question, please consider the following: Since ancient times, everywhere in the world, not only in Europe, there has been a significant frequency of rape; most of them are undoubtedly men, and I find it ridiculous to suggest that the motivation for these acts has nothing to do with the sexuality of the perpetrators. The percentage of male sexual attackers is even higher than the percentage of Muslims among terrorists, the ratio of sexual rapists among men is also higher than terrorists among Muslims, and we also do not have a reliable way to distinguish a man who only has sex with the consent of a woman from one who does not care so much about the voluntariness of intercourse; what about that
Just to be sure, I would like to add that the message of this text should definitely not be: "Let's do nothing." Of course, it is appropriate to defend yourself, the state should stop throwing sticks under the feet of citizens when they want to arm themselves (which, by the way, would help victims of terrorism and rape), and laws should not stand in the way of private discrimination; on the other hand, global persecution of a certain group of people just because they are statistically more at risk is nothing but absolute bullshit, and makes about as much sense in the case of Muslims as it does in the case of men.

In 2011, someone whitewashed Lukáš Kuzmiak's apartment and took his computer from it; however, the person in question also had remote access to it and installed a program on it that allowed him to take screenshots of the screen and watch the webcam. He went with it to the uniformed monkeys, who sent him to the grove, because it is said that this is not a common procedure (that is the reason, of course); so the person in question managed it himself, he finally found the computer, only as part of that he published photos of people who were already using it (even if he put black rectangles over their eyes). Result? Those photographed and published are suing Lukáš Kuzmiak for psychological harm (the court of first instance ordered him to pay almost two hundred thousand; however, both sides appealed against the verdict), so the person in question is facing court battles; and what is the lesson of the story? Don't you dare do the fools' work better than they do; it's not hard, but you're dealing with evil.

The foreign police raided Prague 6, where they found a company with 44 employees, 38 of whom were foreigners, 24 of whom did not have a permit; the owner faces half a year in prison, the illegals are deported, the uniformed monkeys brag about it and the nationalists applaud because Bohemia to Bohemia. And what actually gives so many people a reason to be happy? Well, twenty-four people's lives are going to get worse, their employer is probably going to complain, and their company is going out of business, which will hurt its customers, including potential ones; and the alleged positive? A vacancy in the market can be filled by someone else; what about the fact that it is clearly less preferred by customers (otherwise it would already become a natural market path), but mainly it will be Czech as a log! Is ruining people's lives and making customers worse off really something we should applaud?

The Association of Small and Medium Enterprises mourns the Ministry of Industry to ban hourly spouses from performing more complex tasks, such as bricklaying, plumbing, painting or carpentry; therefore, they should continue to perform only minor tasks such as mowing lawns or cleaning carpets. Why? According to the chairman of the Association of Small and Medium-Sized Entrepreneurs, it is said that hourly spouses take work from self-employed people and, moreover, often do it poorly; and since people are so unbelievably stupid that they still order their services, the state must now come in and protect them by law from the services of the competition and above all from themselves, because that would be the way the craftsman would agree with the client on the terms on which he would do the work for him. And after all... what's wrong with someone "taking away a job" by providing a service that people voluntarily choose, thereby demonstrating that it's a better alternative for them?

Anyone who has ever been on the water can imagine very well how many boaters are constantly under the influence of alcohol; rums in the boat, beers at the stalls, it's almost a tradition. This year, unfortunately, it also happened to the monkeys in uniform, who leafed through the laws and found that the same zero tolerance applies on ships as on cars; and actually even worse, not only the butt nor the hook must be drunk on the canoe, this even applies to the one who just drives like porcelain. So Benga sat down by the Ohri, where the rowers are buzzing and cashing in; there is a fine of up to one hundred thousand (!) crowns for alcohol in the blood on board. Yes, you read that right; I don't give a shit. In the case of road rage, at least the excuse can be made that the drunk driver is a danger to others; but here? It is nothing more than god-awful pandering of more money to people who do nothing to anyone and thus endanger themselves as much as possible with their drunkenness; such a disgusting act would not be acceptable to any entity other than the state.

Anarcho-capitalism is often the target of statist ridicule, according to which it is only a theory that cannot be put into practice; if you start talking in front of them about private courts or something similar to the police, they usually react by pointing out the fact that nowhere is the law handled completely privately, because the state can do it better and it "wouldn't work" at all.
The typical answers of anarcho-capitalists then mostly consist of a theoretical (and mostly absolutely correct) explanation of why and how it could work; however, any such speculations are often dismissed by simply pointing out that nothing of the sort is currently being implemented anywhere, resulting in a debate in which the libertarian defends something and the statist scoffs at it, automatically putting himself in a much more advantageous position.
As things really stand, I find this mode of debate quite absurd; why?
Well, in recent history we got a look at what a centrally controlled economy looks like - and it was appalling. We were also able to see in various states that any economic segment that any state allowed itself to leave to the market began to function better than before; on the contrary, it has probably never happened that the state stopped managing something, which would lead to the fulfillment of all those catastrophic statist predictions about market failure.
Imagine knowing two fundamentally different ways of solving problems; you first try to solve everything with one and it's not very good, then you start to solve individual things with the other and you always get better. Will you then try to maintain the status quo at all costs, or will you try for (further) improvement?
There are essentially two ways to control the course of things: Either let free people act, or have their lives centrally planned by force from the position of the state. So far, central planning has always failed; and each time it was replaced by free market principles, there were positive changes.
So what actually works and what fails? Who should question and who should defend? On whom should the burden of proof lie? So what is theory and what is practice?
The reality is that there are a huge number of industries where the state has failed across the board while the private sector has succeeded; on the contrary, there is probably no industry that thrives in private hands and only begins to flourish thanks to the state.
So based on what empirical experience can anyone claim about something that we need the state to do it because the free market "wouldn't work"?
In a rational discussion uninfluenced by state propaganda, the statist should, on the contrary, explain to the anarchist why this or that sector should be the rare exception that requires a central plan for its functioning.

Croatian Finance Minister Boris Lalovac boasted about how great EET they have there; the state can see how much money entrepreneurs have, how high sales, daily turnover and even what they buy with their money. The tax office watches it all and looks for anomalies, which he then eliminates; the Croatian Finance Minister even boasted that since they know absolutely everything about entrepreneurs (they say they also monitor the physical movement of cash registers, if it occurs), they can manage not only taxes, but even economic activities, i.e. the entire economy - and all this with the help of information obtained from EET. Scary? Why not, if we have that beauty in the Czech Republic too; and that ours doesn't send so much information to the tax office? Well, it is the first version; in fact, in my opinion, the question is not whether the Czech EET will be upgraded to the Croatian form, but rather when it will happen and under what pretexts.

Viktor Tolar, with thirty years of driving experience, lost his driver's license for more than a year, after which he had to take driving school again to get it back at all; why? In three years, he exceeded the speed limit three times in the Strahov Tunnel by less than twenty kilometers per hour, and four times he drove less than sixty in the fifty; add to that "he found it indecent to haggle with the police" and also the merging of the offenses for discussion, which effectively slows down the disappearance of points, and we're painted, well... in this case, scored. I can very vividly imagine all the comments about how stupid the person was acting; and I admit his approach wasn't exactly the height of prudence, on the other hand... is this really the point? Such laws are always defended with talk of safety, but when they are then used to bully, it is so often excused that the bullied did not defend themselves when they could; but do we really want it to be necessary?
In my opinion, the most important question is not at all what most people start to solve in connection with the issue, i.e. whether the revocation of the driver's license in the given case is in accordance with the law, whether any of the officials or police officers made a mistake, or how unwisely the victim of state bullying proceeded, but whether it is okay for the person in question to lose his driver's license for what he committed; and this is not just some anarchist view, here I am talking about the spirit of the law and the alleged reasons why it applies, which should be an argument for statists as well. The question is: On the basis that someone, after thirty years of driving, over the course of three years exceeded the speed limit three times by less than twenty kilometers per hour and four times by less than ten, can it be concluded that the person in question is socially dangerous as a driver and this problem will be solved by a year without a driver's license and driving school? If not, then it just shouldn't happen; regardless of "the law is the law" and the like.

title_en: The police have apologized... after 21 years
text_en:
It was 1995, and then twenty-four-year-old Jaroslava Jelínková came to the police with a fabricated accusation of rape; the description of the perpetrator's car matched the car of a certain Fehim Hanuš (dark-haired with an athletic figure, although the perpetrator was described as a stocky blond), originally from Yugoslavia, so the uniformed monkeys were not lazy and tasked the police to seize it. What about the fact that the gynecologist soon discovered (and let the bengs know) that there were no signs of rape on the subject's body; the fiddlers had most likely already fallen, so nothing happened to the interventionist, so she started the action the next day. They brutally attacked Mr. Hanuš and his son at their home, but they both (quite understandably) defended themselves, so a shootout ensued in which the innocent Fehim Hanuš was literally shot to death - eight bullets in the stomach, two in the head; amazingly he survived! Unfortunately, with life-long consequences, and before they put him together in the hospital, his company went bankrupt.
What about the monkey Jiří Houba, who ordered the intervention? After all: "We were supposed to wait for the perpetrator to rape someone else?" And then? Twenty-one years of court battles for an apology and compensation. Seriously, the uniformed monkeys refused, the Supreme Court sent the case back to the lower court four times in a row, finally even ordering it to be assigned to another judge; after twenty-one years, the court finally decided that the Ministry of Justice should apologize and pay three hundred thousand. And that, dear friends, is the cost of breaking into someone's home, ambushing them, shooting them, maiming them, nearly killing them and ruining their lives... assuming you're wearing the right uniform, the media is pretty cool too; but can you imagine the hype if it was a private event? However, state propaganda is very powerful; lives destroyed by repressive elements simply count differently than lives destroyed by private individuals.

The title certainly does not mean to belittle the tragedy that occurred in Nice on the night of Thursday to Friday, in which dozens of people lost their lives; I just follow the philosophy of life that there is nothing that shouldn't be the subject of humor, so I got inspired
with some funny comments
. What happened is probably well known to everyone: Two sadistic goons got into a truck and drove two kilometers through a crowd of people before being shot by uniformed monkeys. Unsurprisingly, the religion of the two mass murderers became the most popular topic, as if what they did had consequences for other followers of their religion (if it was Islam, which I think is likely); I don't want to imagine what will happen when someone finds out that among the suicide bombers there is an even higher percentage of men than Muslims... we will probably deport the guys away from Europe, safety above all else. However, I will dwell on the method of the attack.
A truck was used for the murder, which makes it pretty clear that when some people are serious about killing others, there are tons of other ways, not necessarily firearms; and this one also seems to be quite effective. There is hardly any serious discussion about the truck ban yet, which is fine; but what about bans and regulation of firearms? Are you arguing that you have nothing to do with it? Well, it comes down to how we look at the whole thing; the attackers managed to drive two kilometers through an unarmed crowd before being shot...how far would they have gone and how many people would they have murdered if all their victims (even the potential ones) had one arm long? How many lives could be saved? And why is it that every time someone uses a firearm to commit a massacre, this fact is constantly highlighted by the media, while silence falls on the sidewalk when such weapons could save lives?

Do you remember what French President François Hollande looks like, especially his hairstyle? Are you wondering why I'm talking about his hair when he doesn't have any clear but this boring politician haircut? Well, his personal hairdresser gets over a quarter mega a month for his work; I'm probably the last person who would mind if someone can earn money, but the person in question receives the money from the state coffers (and his salary, by the way, is about two-thirds of the president's salary; few people would pay that much for a barber... but strangers don't bleed). The publication of the hairdresser's salary caused outrage among the French and the feeling that Hollande was a moron for wasting; But how do they know it's a waste? Well, from their point of view, the expense is not worth what it will bring them (and no wonder); however, the question remains why the overwhelming majority of people advocate subsidizing everything possible, when the very fact that something needs to be subsidized indicates that
people are not worth paying for that thing out of their own money
.

Minister for Regional Development (that's another function) Karla Šlechtová posted on her Facebook profile a heart-wrenching story about how she went to a baroque concert for the anniversary of Charles IV. to some church, from which she was allegedly thrown out by the priest, because the person in question is pushing for the taxation of church restitutions; the person in question requests an explanation from the church as to why it is discriminating against a minister of the Czech government, and at the same time refers to democracy. Let us now leave aside whether this is at all true, for some discrepancies in date and place are shown, which, when pointed out, his comment mysteriously disappears; but let's assume now that it actually happened exactly as the minister describes. If so, is it really something so terrible and condemnable on the part of the church? What actually happened?
The state took property from the church, which after many years was finally recognized as a mistake, as a result of which the decision was made to return the looted property; however, the state wants to take a part of this transaction by force (taxation of restitution), which it creatively justifies by collecting protection money from other transactions as well - this is the first degree of this insolence. The second stage is when the representative of the supporters and promoter of this robbery is surprised that the robbed does not want to play on her property for free; and whining about how the church discriminates and refuses to let a minister of the Czech government to a concert in a democratic country, as if it should be some kind of duty. The worst thing about the whole thing is that the absurdity of the whole thing does not occur to the person in question, because in her eyes robbery is not robbery if it is legislated, and whoever organizes the concert must not deny entry to anyone, because discrimination (it's bad, yes) and also "it's just not done".

Ever since the results of the referendum on the (non)remaining of Great Britain in the EU are known, political negotiation dances have begun on the topic of who needs mutual trade more, the British or the rest of Europe; there are various statements and speculations about what the EU will "enable" for British citizens in terms of trade, which is also related to various pro-Union arguments on the topic of how, thanks to the Union, we can move goods and people very freely. Nothing but shit, I tell you! The reality is that one gang of thugs from national governments has set up absolutely senseless barriers to free people to trade, while another – transnational – gang has changed them to make them a little more tolerable; then we have to pay all these robber clans under the threat of violence from our own resources in the form of protection money - called taxes.
So, the next time you hear from some moron in a tie, whose paycheck you're trying to parasitize, about how European officials will "allow" us to trade and how we need some bureaucrats and politicians to remove barriers to free trade, remember that there are naturally no such barriers here, because when two people want to exchange goods, they would just naturally do so; the reason why it sometimes presents a problem is definitely not the people, but the politicians, who already feel that they have the right to a commission from the trade that they did not deserve and are only complicating it, so the solution to such a situation is clearly simply to stop messing with it, but certainly not to establish another apparatus of exactly the same profiteers, which will mitigate the effects of what the first ones did, at the cost of clouds of bureaucracy and other regulations. The claim that these bureaucrats are "enabling" us to trade is absolute bullshit.

Some of the EU scumbags have been spinning metaphysical nonsense lately about robotics and artificial beings they call "electronic persons"; robots are said to already be at a fairly high level of autonomy, so a legal framework needs to be devised and implemented for them. What else to expect from the EU? Regulate potentially future artificial autonomous creatures before they are even made; that makes sense after all, we have to think ahead right? But then it was discovered that headless regulation at all costs was not the only reason; it turns out that social insurance for robots is the primary goal. Seriously, this is no joke; social insurance has been found to cause people to be replaced by machines, so the "logical" step according to the EU is to tax those machines. By debating the proposal, the European Parliament is making clear what every libertarian has known for a long time: Social security is simply a tax; it has nothing to do with any social security or insurance.

After what
avalanche
stupid ones
ideas
from Marx
she stopped for a moment, the person in question had probably made up her mind
to inspire in Brno
; the person in question now wants to force municipalities by law to provide social housing for their poor and homeless because... well, because simply socialism. Rob everyone, squander the loot, squander it, embezzle it and give the rest to someone else, show activity, buy votes and maybe still feel good about yourself; that's probably how Marks works, because she probably doesn't realize that in the end, by giving away something "for free" she will harm not only a part of those she gives it to, but also especially all the others who are afraid that they could end up in such a situation. How is that? Well, it reduces the benefits of responsible behavior and mitigates the natural bad consequences of irresponsible behavior; and this, unfortunately, is the inevitable consequence of all socialist measures -
willy-nilly they produce irresponsible people
.

It's fascinating how many people automatically feel that those in power are somehow professionally or expertly qualified to make decisions; the state deliberately builds this aura for them to convince citizens that the decision makers know better than they do what is best for them. Even if we leave aside that even for those who are apparently qualified, the whole thing is nothing but a myth, a political game and an illusion, sometimes it is possible to install someone in a position so masterfully that it makes one's head spin; for example, the mayor of Brno currently has Matěj Hollan, a musician without a driver's license (who never even had one), as his deputy for transport. But what about the fact that traffic in the second largest city of the Czech Republic will be decided by someone who has never even driven in it? After all, the main thing is the political affiliation – the Live Brno movement with the support of the Pirates; inu, such a socialist return to the roots... before 1989, personnel opinion was also more important than professional knowledge.

The holidays are starting, which affects a good part of us in some way, whether it is school children, their parents, university students, teachers, visitors to various festivals and the like; traffic to article (even non-article) and comment sites is down, but my schedule will also be a bit affected by the holidays. For that reason, I'm switching Stoky into vacation mode for two months, which means:
1/ Texts may not be published here with such regularity as before; there will be an effort, but I don't know how successful it will be.
2/ I am asking libertarians who have more time for texts to Stok; email them to me (or publish them yourself; ideally with a date in the future so I can include them).
3/ Everyone who discusses with me in e-mails should be understanding for slower responses; I enjoy the discussion, but I won't be on the computer that much.
4/ My participation in discussions in Stoká will be limited; when you write something here, don't count on me always reading it (although I probably will most of the time).

The company Elektra PV operated the most popular e-shop of 2015; but that's over now. Why? Well, one of its two hundred and fifty suppliers (or maybe one of their suppliers) didn't pay VAT, which the tax office solved in its own way - before investigating the situation, he froze the assets and accounts of this company with a twenty-five-year history and a billion-dollar turnover, without letting anyone know anything (the owner had to ask for the reason and was only told the next day); Elektra PV was therefore completely paralyzed out of nowhere and without the ability to pay suppliers or deliver orders, it has no other option than to end its activities, because such a large company cannot be kept alive under the given conditions. One hundred and twenty people will lose their jobs, countless customers will have to wait for their orders, and suppliers will be wiped out for payments; great job, Financial Administration! Because if there was no state, who would liquidate e-shops?

Last week you
they could finish reading in Stoké
, that although I support Brexit, I do not believe in it very strongly; and now I can only state that it was a pleasant mistake. And what can we see around us now that less than 52% of the British voters voted for Brexit? Among the less interesting things, for example, David Cameron's speech, which was surprisingly classy for a robber in a jacket who lives on hard-earned money (which wouldn't be so strange; after all, he has people to write to him), but mainly in which he, as an opponent of Brexit, announced his resignation from his post, so that Britain will be led out of the EU by someone who agrees with it (which I am surprised by the ability to accept defeat; but I have a tendency to words don't trust politicians too much, so we'll see what happens); absolutely unsurprising are the speeches of Brexit opponents across the Internet, as well as their criticism from those who would have reacted exactly the same if the referendum had gone the other way.
However, I consider more interesting, for example, the petition for the announcement of the second referendum and other tweets or hints of a similar type that we can follow; I would probably not take things like that seriously, but I am concerned about the restarted Maastricht referendum in Denmark in 1992, the adoption of the euro despite the results of the 2000 referendum there, the two restarted referendums on the Nice and Lisbon treaties in Ireland in 2001 and 2008, the planned acceptance of the euro in Sweden after it was rejected by the 2003 referendum, the two the referendums on the European Constitution in Holland and France in 2005 or the one on the rescue package in Greece in 2015. And even though in Britain it seems that the referendum will be respected and the nonsense about non-binding and petitions about repetition are not taken seriously, I tend to believe it on the whole, but certainly not without reservation. Do you think my skepticism is misplaced?

title_en: A small fleeting victory of freedom
text_en: The US Senate showed a flicker of common sense; vetoed a shitstorm of four consecutive gun-restricting bills. It probably won't surprise anyone that the Democrats will try to use the Orlando massacre for their prohibitionist desires; this time, however, the Republicans also shined and showed that they are exactly the same bunch of prohibitionists - the golden nail was John Cornyn's proposal, which demanded that the sale of weapons to people suspected of terrorism be delayed for 72 hours... beware, not convicted, suspected! The purpose of those 72 hours was to allow the authorities to make an effort and get a judge to ban the purchase completely; the meaning of such a measure then completely escapes me even in the intentions of statist logic and morality - if the court did not prohibit the suspect in question from owning a weapon until the moment he went to buy it, how can he reconsider this decision only on the basis that the person in question does so? Or, "You may buy a gun as long as you don't want to buy one." Fortunately, that was too much even for the senators (that is, for about half of them).

Today there will be a referendum in Britain on its exit from the EU; the vast majority of the establishment (understood and unsurprisingly led by the disgraced Cameron from the Tories) are of course freaking out about this and scaring the British people that this will be a fatal and irreversible decision that will basically be a disaster for their lives, but fortunately there are (even in Cameron's party) opposing views. At first, the official line scored points, then the situation turned and the Brexit option became more popular, but in the end the murder of Jo Cox was skilfully used for another twist in preferences - it was enough to indicate her connection with the supporters of Brexit, which I consider exceptionally retarded, because on the one hand they wouldn't help themselves, but above all, even if they did, how is the murder of a politician related to whether membership in the EU is beneficial for the British? Well, let's see what the vote tallies will bring in the end; what do you think Personally, I understandably support Brexit, but I don't believe in it very strongly.

title_en: DJ Trump, the King of Flies!
text_en:
You don't really need Donald John Trump
to represent
, but still I find it strange how many libertarians have some sympathy for this lover of totalitarianism - maybe Molyneux's talk is to blame, maybe just some repressed base desires to hurt people; whatever the reason, I'd like to reiterate here what DJ Trump is - no "fighter against the system", but a statist aspiring to a police state. After the Orlando massacre, he let it be known that Americans who don't snap at their neighbors should go snap; specifically about Omar Mateen's neighbors, he stated that because they noticed his strange behavior, receiving many packages in a short period of time, an increased amount of time spent in the garage and did not report any of this, they should face consequences, serious consequences, and do some jail time. I honestly cannot imagine how a candidate with such an attitude could be acceptable to any libertarian.
But if only a libertarian! After all, it all contradicts even common sense; yes, it sounds dramatic when it comes to DJ Trump's speech, but it lacks even a hint of logic. How could something like this work in practice? Sure, Omar Mateen was behaving strangely before the attack, spending time in the garage and receiving a large number of packages; but how many other people show the exact same symptoms and then do nothing? How is the cracking supposed to work? I have a strange neighbor, I report him to the authorities, who will do what? Will they make a record? Or are they going to check him out, how big of a fool is he? How many millions of people would need to be framed across America if all citizens seriously behaved as DJ Trump is asking? And what would that mean in practice? Extreme restrictions on the freedom of practically everyone, huge financial expenses and no real results at all; or does anyone really believe that terrorists can be eliminated this way?

An unknown thief stole an expensive bicycle, he was caught on camera, the owner quite understood that uniformed monkeys are useless in such a case (and anyone who has ever reported a theft to them certainly understands the reason), so he decided to spread the video among people on his own axis in the hope that the goons can be identified; however, the state intervened, helped a little, saved a little - the Office for the Protection of Personal Data intervened to defend the rogue, and the Supreme Court complied; in the judgment it is written: "The purpose of operating camera systems for the protection of property is not (in short) to take records for their future publication, but only for the eventual transfer to the designated authorities for further actions. The investigation and prosecution of criminal activity (which can also include the commission of misdemeanors) is at the same time fully within the competence of state authorities." Is there anything else that needs to be added? I think not.

"Gun licenses should only be issued in emergency situations. I don't think there's any reason why people should carry guns." Jiří Dienstbier, minister for nothing and at the same time the biggest nonsense, flashed this totalitarian statement some time ago; and after the Orlando massacre, of course, the socan in question didn't miss the opportunity to add his spit, although it's quite obvious that a moron who goes to shoot up a gay bar certainly won't stop a gun ban (if only because a far more fundamental ban on killing people didn't stop him), while a couple of tough gays with one long arm would eliminate him quite reliably, so he'd only have time to shoot a couple of them, or - at best - the shit who although he dared the unarmed, he was deterred only by the fact that his victims would fight back and not give in so easily.
Dienstbier commented on the massacre by saying: "I take every such attack as evidence that weapons belong only to the security forces of the state. They do not belong to any imaginary militias, they do not belong to the hands of the public who are afraid," while completely ignoring that precisely because of the absence of weapons in the hands of the victims, one sadistic lunatic who always gets hold of a weapon is enough to do such damage, because the famous security forces of the state simply will not prevent it, because even if they were everywhere five minutes is enough time for a massive bloodbath if the victims cannot effectively defend themselves. Not to mention that disarming the population by the state is a hallmark of any totalitarian regime; after all, Dienstbier's rhetoric is nothing new: "Germans who want to use arms should join the SA or SS; ordinary citizens do not need arms because they are useless in the hands of the state." – Heinrich Himmler

I have been here less than six weeks
reported his broken arm
a
quite soon also about her miraculous straightening
; because the healing was going great thanks to my perfect mental state, it seemed like the cast would come off after a month, but the pitchfork got in the way a bit when I moved my hand (even in the cast) quite carelessly and basically broke it again... but just like the first time it was worth it and I have no regrets xD
After less than six weeks, the cast finally came off; for a moment I was disappointed that the hand was strangely stiff. However, after arriving from the plaster room to the doctor's office, the doctor could not believe his eyes when I gave him the volcanic greeting "live long and prosper" (the worst fractures are on the bones leading to the middle finger and ring finger) - he said he expected such mobility as I have now only after a month of rehabilitation; it's true, I'm still not completely done with my hand, but it's getting better hour by hour.
The only downside is that when I clench my fingers into my palm, my ring finger comes out of my hand and crosses my little finger, which is a bit of a problem when typing with all ten, effectively I only have nine now (the ring finger on the keyboard is the same as the little finger; both fingers press the same key), but luckily I have a master skill, so
513 flawless keystrokes per minute
I will give even now; more than enough for Stoky and work xD
It's a bit problematic for me now to work with the mouse - which will get better soon - and to grasp things (because when I hold something, my ring finger rests on my pinky) - which will probably stay that way; Well, considering how wonderful my life is and what God has given me, I'd say that a slightly crippled hand is still a pretty small disadvantage to my overall existence compared to all the advantages. All I have to do is state that I'm still a pretty satisfied bastard; now just to fully rock it, but if I'm already giving what I should after a month of rehab on the first day, I suppose it could be eaf. Thanks to everyone for the help in Stoky and especially elsewhere. 110

Since you usually read about bad things in the Sewers, this time it will be my pleasure to inform you about something positive as well: In Texas, the more than a century-old repression that forbids the visible carrying of firearms by its residents, which could now change, so that those who do not threaten anyone or threaten anyone with a weapon, will be allowed to carry it visibly, even in their hand; in addition, the ban on carrying weapons on college campuses could end. These changes might deter some criminals from committing violence, or at least make it more difficult for them, but above all it is a step towards freedom; the state should not have anything to interfere with people where they want to carry a weapon (or any other thing of theirs), nor how and with what they will defend themselves against criminals who do not respect similar laws anyway, so they arm themselves despite the bans. I would like our legislators to be inspired by Texas in this direction.

Two Afghans living in Sweden had a brilliant idea - they took an airsoft gun and went to rob people, thinking that in the dark no one would know the difference anyway; until they came across a victim who either wasn't fooled or judged the situation as hopeless, pulled out a knife and crushed them (one forever). A meritorious act? Well, he must not go unpunished; and so the local court sentenced the assault victim to two years in prison for unreasonable self-defense with a brilliant comment - the assaulted should not have defended himself, but should have tried to run away, and I wonder how the smart judge would have run away from bullets in a similar situation. Above all, I do not understand the twisted logic when the victim, who eliminated the attacker so well that he will never be able to repeat his attack on anyone, instead of being awarded, receives a punishment, especially one as senseless and beastly as
prison
.

Czech Television has stepped on the so-called "non-payers", chasing them through the courts in order to get even more cinders; and who are the culprits? Well, they include anyone who dares to brazenly buy electricity without giving an affidavit that they don't own a TV; even if we leave aside the sky-high audacity of automatically forcing fees from practically everyone who does not do something, the ownership of a television receiver is in any case by law a reason to pay, completely regardless of whether the owner in question watches ČT. Forcing subjects to pay for services (and especially state propaganda, whether in education or in the media) that they do not receive and do not use is such a specialty of the state; usually, however, it has some kind of cover story about the apocalypse that would occur without the state, while at CT nobody even bothered to come up with any more - do you have a television? Pay!

The French socialist comrades came up with another brilliant idea of what to ban again; this time it's about broadcasting and watching European Championship football matches on big screens in bars. Why? That is evident; due to the threat of terrorist attacks. Televisions in bars will be replaced by state-run fan zones, guarded by buffoons; the result will be that, in addition to the profits that the bar owners will lose, the whole fun will cost the taxpayers more than two hundred million crowns. I don't want to go into too much detail about what security results this solution will lead to (although I strongly doubt its effectiveness); the important thing is that even if they really made it safer, it is not an argument for such repression. If we accepted this rhetoric as our own, we could then proceed in exactly the same way in the case of all other dangerous entertainment.

title_en: The EU is also against weapons in the Czech Republic
text_en:
As probably most readers are well aware, gun legislation in the Czech Republic is less terrible and disgusting than in most European countries; some even euphemistically describe this state of affairs by saying that we have good gun laws. I personally do not agree with such an assessment, because until weapons are sold without registration, permits, restrictions and in anonymity, this is repression and the initiation of violence by the state; pseudo-arguments based on catastrophic scenarios, that in such a case people would kill themselves en masse, do not stand up primarily because if people really wanted to kill themselves, they could do it without legally regulated firearms. No one, except a few deranged individuals, wants to risk their own life so that they can kill the people around them; but when such a person is found and acquires a weapon (which he can do even now, only more difficult), he does far more damage in an unarmed society than in an armed one.
To my considerable surprise, it seems that Czech politicians don't even have extremely pro-prohibition appetites regarding gun legislation (that is, compared to the politicians of other European countries); I have no doubt that if voices could be raised from it, opinions would be easily corrected, but so far this is not happening. However, where there is no fuss at the national level, the EU will push it; and it seems that it will be exactly the same with weapons: the new directive regulates weapons with magazines, revolvers with non-removable magazines less strictly; and although the Czech politicians are quite dismissive of this invention, it will probably not be of any use to them, as the other member states are playfully overriding them... in other words, exactly what the propagandists constantly told us before joining the EU will happen - we will lose absolutely basic freedoms from above.

That's how the customs officials were looking for refugees on the train once (wet dreams of Islam killers are coming true) and lo and behold, what did they not come across? A business traveler took nine kilos of ecstasy and a kilo of cocaine as a bonus; although the person in question did not attack anyone and did not violate anyone's property rights, uniformed and legalized robbers not only took seven to eight megacrowns worth of goods from his brother, but unlike ordinary thieves, they also plan to keep the poor man in a cage called prison for eight to twelve years and limit his freedom there. And for what? The person in question simply drove people
goods for which they are willing to pay
, but the rulers do not like it; such an action is not fundamentally different from a moral point of view than when you mug someone on the street, take millions from them and put them in the basement for part of their life for fun... yet most people applaud it only because it was sanctioned by the paps, whom the person in question typically does not even respect.

The European Commission, together with Internet giants such as Google, Facebook and Twitter, published a code of conduct on the Internet, the aim of which is to prevent hate speech; if it was a voluntary action on the part of those companies, it is of course only their business how they handle their business and who they give space to express their opinions, but if it was coercion under the threat of sanctions from the European Union, it is
gross suppression of freedom of speech
. Since many do not see a very significant difference (in both cases it is censorship), I will explain it: If a private media owner censors his content, he is only deciding on something that is his (just as everyone decides who to let talk in their living room at home) and customers can reject it; if this censorship is carried out by the state, it is a violent intervention in someone else's property and typically global oppression, since the laws usually apply generally to everyone (that is, all the media, and competition does not work).
So the very fundamental question is: How did the negotiations between the European Commission and the aforementioned corporations take place? I can imagine the pressure, because in the past we have already been able to verify that the EU can throw legislative rubbish under the feet of even big giants; on the other hand, I wouldn't even be surprised if the management of those corporations was made up of indoctrinated people who simply accepted European propaganda as their own - after all, there are not a lot of such people in the world. I also wouldn't be shocked by a scenario where the European Commission would offer some benefits to those big players, but I don't think it's very likely; in such cases, the state typically offers to suppress competition, which is not very effective in the web environment, moreover, it does not bring political points, as people are quite adamant about restricting the freedom of the Internet. Which option do you think is the most likely, dear readers? Leave your opinions in the comments.

The Ostrava tax office decided to harass the Raptor company a bit; withheld her VAT refunds while an investigation into alleged carousel fraud was underway, which was never proven. The catch, however, is that such behavior is not only grossly immoral, but even illegal; so the Raptor company turned to the court, which ruled in their favor and ordered the bastard to return the loot with interest, which, however, this predatory organization refused to pay, which made it a funny thing to be foreclosed on (well, it was funny, if we forget that we pay for it all from taxes). However, I do not consider the worst part of the whole thing to be the fact that the state essentially imposes the seizure (distraint) on itself, but rather the officials' desire to do harm, which reached such proportions that the tax office openly disregarded laws and court decisions; and unfortunately this is far from the first such case in recent times when
state agencies blatantly ignore the law
, with which they otherwise kill subjects.

Although we often hear many civil servants chattering against home births, these are still surprisingly legal under Czech legislation; however, there is a small catch - you can give birth at home, but without a midwife. Dark humor? No, reality. Home births are said to be too dangerous, so let's make it better by banning women in labor from professional care; you ask why I also asked, but the only answer that comes to mind is the need for the state to make home births even more dangerous, so that the necessity of our socialist healthcare system will be revealed and the fertile ground for another ban will be prepared; when do you think it will arrive? And while we're at it, we can also make domestic conception illegal right away; it would play so that everyone can fuck as he likes!

I'm not much of a fan of hip-hop, but I can't help but mention a couple of verses that the group Chaozz came up with years ago: "And who makes wars? Well, politicians! They're the only ones who deserve a shotgun; or a gun, because they're the only ones who want wars - normal people better sleep in peace." There is a great truth hidden in those verses, which is confirmed, for example, by the events of the Western Front at Christmas 1914; in the trenches, millions of young men who had never even seen each other before, yet under the influence of state propaganda, killed each other completely senselessly... however, at Christmas 1914, their nature won out over indoctrination: That in many places throughout the front, hundreds of thousands of soldiers maintained peace of arms during the holidays, probably will not surprise anyone very much; however, thousands to tens of thousands of them even celebrated Christmas together - the men left the trenches, gave each other gifts with the "enemies", sang carols, treated the wounded together, celebrated Christmas.
Because something like this was quite a powerful experience for most of the participants, they confided about it in letters from the front, which already aroused public interest, some newspapers even wrote about it; when it came to the senior army officers, they quite unsurprisingly behaved like pigs - the units that "guilted" were transferred elsewhere (for example, from the Western to the Eastern Front) and in general, military units began to be moved with the aim of preventing the soldiers from establishing relations with the "enemy", because the state simply needs to awaken the worst in people and eliminate all the good. Despite these efforts, however, those goons failed to completely bury humanity, as similar incidents occurred in the later years of the war; however, the truth is that, unfortunately, nothing similar has ever been repeated on such a scale.

Although libertarians usually do not call for the expansion of the state's powers, in the case of closing borders to refugees, I see relatively many exceptions around me, justified approximately as follows: "If we had more freedom (the legal possibility to effectively defend our property, privately discriminate on the basis of religion, etc.), we could afford to let refugees into the territory of the Czech Republic; however, since we do not have these freedoms and, moreover, redistribution is raging, the state should close and guard the borders, possibly ban Islam.” What is pernicious about this thinking? Instead of calling for a reduction in the power of the state, we want to strengthen it so that the government can repair the damage it has caused through its regulations; this is a notorious statist trap that we can see everywhere - for example, the creation of the unemployed through increasing the price of labor (various employee protections, the minimum wage, etc.) and the subsequent "fight against unemployment" by further distorting the market.
Another logical flaw in this argument should be seen better than anyone else by libertarians; it is indeed possible (and I also assume it) that in a free society people would currently cope with the situation surrounding the immigration crisis by natural free market discrimination (whether at work, in the provision of services, or in closed communities, the possible form of which can be found in the works of Hans-Hermann Hoppe), but we cannot know for sure, because
the market would perhaps come up with a different solution
. So when we want the state to keep refugees outside the borders, we are actually predicting the behavior of free people in the sense of: "They would deal with immigrants one way or another, so let's simulate it with state interventions." In essence, it is like declaring that if there is likely to be some charity and solidarity in the free market, then state redistribution is perfectly fine, because it actually simulates these free market mechanisms.

Both the Parliament and the Senate approved the amendment to the Food Law; what can we look forward to? Another buzz, how else; this time, the cigarette manufacturers were in the spotlight, and thus indirectly their clients – all smokers. Once again, the embarrassing warning about the dangers of smoking on every box will increase; now it will have to occupy up to 65% of the surface area of the packaging, and in addition it will contain disgusting images of dead children or sick people, as we know from some other countries. Unfortunately, that's not all; it will also be prohibited to manufacture and sell flavored cigarettes. For a limited time, there will initially be an exemption for menthol cigarettes; however, even these will disappear from the shelves over time. Since the law passed both houses of parliament very smoothly, I do not think that the situation can be expected to improve in the foreseeable future.
The purpose of this measure should, in theory, be to protect the health of the population, which is why absolutely barbaric interventions in our freedoms are so often excused lately. Many people object that the state should and must take care of the health of its citizens, because we have socialist health insurance, as a result of which one's health is another's business. However, such an argument should not be used to defend an even greater amount of state intervention, because its consistent application leads to complete absurdities, for example, that the state should decide on the diet of each of us with regard to his health; the only reasonable solution, of course, is to abolish forced health care cost-sharing once and for all and move smoothly to
healthcare model, where everyone makes their own decisions about their care
.

Today we are going to look at an extremely interesting court ruling in Italy; he decided that stealing food is not a crime when you are hungry. The judge acquitted the thirty-six-year-old Ukrainian homeless man who stole from the local supermarket, saying that no one should starve in a civilized country. Not that all existing states were not founded and directly financed by large-scale robbery, but until now they pretended to be something else and at least symbolically declared that one should not steal; in Italy, however, they already gave a shit about that and in some cases they even allowed the subjects to steal. If you're poor enough, you can steal, supposedly so you don't starve. Considering the price of food in our "western world", however, it is not so difficult not to starve, as begging for food is not a problem in principle.
However, even if they were indeed individuals already starving, approving their thefts sets a dangerous precedent; every homeless person can then get rid of some begging and just start stealing, if the court acquits him anyway. Something like this is an unacceptable interference with the property rights of shop owners. It can be assumed that if this practice grew to mass proportions, the courts would probably begin to decide differently, but it would be difficult to compensate for the damage that will occur in the meantime (starting with this small theft). So let's hope that the Czech judges, at least for the time being, will have enough sense not to commit anything similar here.

The Ministry of Transport is planning another piece of bullshit: Novice drivers will have a probationary license for two years, during which they can be penalized for just eight points, which is one serious offense and one seatbelt or phone; then they will have to go to driving schools again, many of them will certainly accept this measure with gratitude. Not to mention that she is alone at all
the existence of driver's licenses does not make much sense
, such ideas are exactly grist to the mill of democratic "justice", which consists in the majority terrorizing the minority; and because there aren't too many novice drivers waiting for the driving school in the population, moreover, they often don't even have the right to vote, which makes them an ideal target for democratic bullying, which Ťok really enjoys, as we've seen many times before. What to add? Don't forget that it
what is legal is far from being right
.

In February, the Ministry of Transport gave birth to an amendment to the law, according to which uniformed monkeys are allowed to confiscate drivers' technicians right on the spot, where they become prosecutors and judges in one person. to collect; and what the hell he didn't want, the decree is here! In what cases can buzzing occur? There are a lot of them, but a random one is, for example, missing exhaust parts, rusty bodywork, leaking operating fluids, too worn brake discs, excessive corrosion and the like; do you notice how incredibly subjective most of these glitches are? For example, when are brake discs "too" worn?
The practical implications of this amendment may be unfathomable; taking into account the above-mentioned subjectivity and the position of uniformed monkeys in the position of judges, against whom there is no appeal on the spot (if they decide to remove the technician even if everything is unequivocally and indisputably fine, you are still unlucky, you have to leave the car standing and demand corrections retroactively), it will be extremely easy to blackmail drivers to do whatever the authority decides - especially this will be applicable to cases in which the monkey means fine, while the driver would like to defend himself in administrative proceedings. I can totally hear it: "Yes, of course it's your right, you don't have to testify, but I can see a little rust here... are you in a big hurry? So you don't have to leave the car here for us; but we're human, I'm sure we'll work something out, it's not worth the few hundred to you."

title_en: The EU is churning out more bans
text_en:
It's been a few years since the European Union, in its infinite wisdom, banned us from selling powerful vacuum cleaners, which no doubt saved the world, but it's not won and more needs to be done; So the European Commission will heroically ban even more things - kettles, toasters and hair dryers that don't fit the imagination of all-knowing officials. At first glance, it may seem that such a solution will bring savings in electricity consumption, so the result will be that everyone saves; that's true, but no one cares too much about the costs on the part of the manufacturers, who will have to stop production of already tried models of goods and start developing new ones. But who can decide if it's worth it? There is really only one way: Let free individuals trade in a free market; people always prefer in voluntary transactions to
what is convenient for them
. Any effort by bureaucrats
it can only make the situation worse
.
The funny thing about the whole thing is that the European paps themselves apparently understand how popular their bans are likely to be; the entire proposal has long been drawn up, its implementation is just waiting for the referendum on Great Britain's withdrawal from the European Union to take place. Long live propaganda and political marketing!

You are right about Erdogan's hypersensitivity about himself
in Stoká they could finish reading earlier
; however, at that time it was still limited to suppressing freedom of expression in Turkey, which has now changed. As? Well, he went whining to Germany, where, surprisingly, he was heard. What happened? When the German satirist Jan Böhmermann composed and delivered a very vulgar poem about Erdogan, in which he certainly did not use napkins, the reaction of the establishment did not take long; the court in Hamburg quickly removed Böhmermann. First, the person in question is forbidden to recite his poem in public, and secondly, he faces six months in prison and a fine of some seven million crowns. The alarming thing about the whole thing is that this time it was not a decision of a Turkish court, but a German one, which judged according to the local "law".
Many - and especially Islamobies - would surely comment now on how weak Europe is giving way to the Islamic world; however, I don't think that this would be the problem, because the law according to which Böhmermann is tried and most likely sentenced existed in Germany long before Erdogan's whining. In short, it is forbidden to insult the heads of foreign states, which I consider to be an absolutely absurd law, which is most likely a kind of remnant from the Middle Ages, when even a simple subject was not allowed to open his mouth to the king; although we are now pretending to be an advanced civilization that respects freedom of speech, when it comes down to it, we are no less barbarians than our ancestors or many members of eastern states - such as the above-mentioned Turkey. If it is about the state showing its power and supremacy over the citizen, no punishment is mild enough.

title_en: Fizzy luxury on someone else's property
text_en: The Home Office is going through hell; built a recreation center for its fiddlers, whose swimming pool, tennis courts and mini-golf course are located on someone else's property. How did this happen? The State Land Office issued these plots in restitution to the original owners, but somehow forgot to inform the Ministry of the Interior; it is great to know that only top experts work in the state administration. However, I find another thing most absurd about the whole case: the Ministry of the Interior intends to solve the whole situation by going to court with the owners of the land, because it wants to use these spaces for its own purposes. Isn't that comical? The very ministry that should theoretically be responsible for maintaining and enforcing the law in this country has invaded someone's property and instead of admitting its mistake, is trying to force through the courts that it is actually okay; are you then surprised by people who believe state propaganda when they behave similarly?

title_en: The "natural" authority of the uniformed monkeys
text_en: MPs approved the government's bill on liability for offences; what would you say it probably contained? That's right, it's about further tightening of the screws, repression and increasing fines, sometimes up to tenfold. I will not deal with all aspects of this amendment here, but only the one that most interested me: You will now pay up to ten thousand crowns for insulting a police officer or official. Why probably? Well, considering the kind of material the state employs in its ranks, it's no wonder that the person in question doesn't enjoy much respect among normal, decent people; it must be clear to anyone with half a brain that no amount of fines, no matter how high, will fix this. However, a more interesting question is why subjects are not allowed to curse and insult state representatives at all, when it has no practical impact on their work and insults are generally not punishable. In reality, it is nothing more than another tool for propaganda, gaining power and flamboyantly showing superiority.

You could read about Petar Hampl in Stoky several times; I consider him to be probably the most disgusting totalitarian on our near-political scene; and not only because, according to his own words, I should be hunted down like a hunted game and executed without trial. He originally began his as-yet-unpromising political career in Svobodny, from which he left after failing to transform this thoroughly right-wing party into a totalitarian law enforcement entity; from there, he left for a better Bloc against Islam, which entered into a coalition with Dawn, which, however, later turned out to be
was (again) tunnelled
. When he discovered that wheat would not flourish here either, he set out to found a new party with the rather comical name Alternative for the Czech Republic.
Although Hampl personally and on behalf of his political groups presents himself as a right-winger and a supporter of individual freedoms, nothing could be further from the truth; after all, what free-thinking person wants to strengthen the powers of the state, close borders, introduce thought crimes (the ban on religion), speak out against wealth inequality, and quite seriously propose abolishing fares on state buses and trains, which would essentially mean the elimination of private transport for some kind of social engineering goal - to get people from the cities to the villages, in fact, just because Hampel thinks it's a good idea. If you happen to doubt, find the program Hamplovo tempo on the Internet, where all these and many other suggestions are presented quite seriously. Those who might be thinking about choosing Alternative for the Czech Republic as a right-wing party should remember these Hampl ideas.

A week ago I you
informed about damage to my hand
and asked for help with writing; first of all, thank you to everyone who contributed their lyrics, but also to everyone who expressed their support. Perhaps because of this, I can happily announce that I was met with such a small miracle: When I arrived at the hospital for a planned operation, the doctor sent me for an X-ray and could not believe his eyes, because where the bones were still scattered on Saturday, he saw everything anatomically aligned, which they say does not happen in principle; long live accelerated healing abilities as a result of a happy mind.
What next? Unfortunately, I have to have my arm in a cast for another five weeks. In connection with this, my request to all authors to keep sending their texts continues; only now it's not such an urgent request, because here I have a sexy slave who I can dictate my thoughts to and she writes them for me xD
Thanks and enjoy life like me.

In recent days I have learned again that life has more imagination than we carry in our dreams; i just broke a few bones in my hand in the process, unfortunately pretty bad, so i'll have to have surgery to straighten them out and keep my hand (hopefully) usable... anyways it was worth it xD
Why are you writing this? Because I would like to make the readers aware of the following:
1/ Writing and working slowly with one hand, so Stoky will probably stagnate a bit; and maybe there won't be a new text every weekday for a while (but maybe something will come out, I have a hot typist to dictate; I just don't have enough time).
2/ I will not participate in discussions.
3/ I will be grateful to other authors if they help me with writing; send your contributions with the publication date a day or two in advance, I'll try to coordinate them.
4/ When the swelling subsides, which according to the doctor will be about Wednesday, I will go into surgery, so I won't even be here until at least Friday.

In a city the size of Prague, there is always someone who takes a spray paint or marker and scribbles something somewhere, typically on someone else's property; it was never given too much importance, until a few politicians decided to make themselves visible by removing anti-refugee signs, so during the last weeks it started to be solved, who scribbles where swastikas and similar nonsense - the first suspects were, of course, Nazis and Islamobies, but soon false flag operation theories appeared, but false false flag operation theories are already visible. Everything is analyzed - the medium used, the placement of the inscriptions, the writer's vocabulary (Islamobes typically do not use the term refugee, but migrant and worse) and other aspects, just to find out whether "the sunbathers are behind it" or "it is the action of Islamophobic"; even this joke was created on the given topic: Why does a right-wing extremist wear a hood when spraying? To keep his dreadlocks from falling into his face.
Are you waiting for the big reveal of the truth? Well, you will most likely see it, but probably differently than you hope; because I have the feeling that everyone from both irreconcilable camps has gone so crazy with collective guilt that they miss the fact that they are actually arguing about shit. Regardless of whether an ardent hate free activist or a die-hard IVČRN fan scribbled it there, it is the action of a few individuals at most; yes, a photo of Stropnický with a spray bottle in his hand would certainly be an absolute hit for Islam killers, and a similar picture of Hampl for a Prague cafe - but why? So that the group to which the sprayer did not belong can claim that "they" did it; those "they", none of whom, apart from units or very small dozens of people, had any idea about the whole event, let alone could participate in any way. Please recover! Of course, other people's property should be inviolable, but here it was damaged by at most a few individuals, not everyone whose views you disagree with.

title_en: Public transport in Blanca? Not by chance; people would go there!
text_en:
What does a market entity do when it finds an opportunity to satisfy the needs of a large number of people? He rejoices, grabs her by the scruff of the neck and earns. How will a public administration with a monopoly in a given industry react in the same situation? He starts looking for reasons not to do anything. How is that? Well, he'll get his money anyway (people will be forced to pay protection money), so why do the extra if there's no profit? It is quite logical that whoever gets more money the better he serves people has a great incentive to provide the best possible service; however, those who receive money regardless of what they actually do for others are mainly motivated to do as little as possible. Despite how obvious these principles are, masses of people can pretend they don't exist under the influence of state propaganda; I would therefore like to give an example from practice that clearly shows how things are.
Do you remember how, before the opening of Blanka, politicians promised that public transport would run there? Well, Blanka has been standing for some time and still nothing; Why not? The transport companies came up with a surprisingly honest rationale: If public transport buses started using the tunnel, these lines would become very popular and a huge number of people would want to ride them; but the operation of so many buses is simply too expensive, so as part of public transport savings, they will not run through Blanka. Yes, you read that right, public transport doesn't go through Blanka because it would just be too good. By consistently applying this logic, we end up canceling the most desirable lines and opening up some obscure ones that no one wants to ride; on the contrary, a consistent rejection of such an approach means a free market – entrepreneurs will be motivated to operate exactly those lines for which people are willing to pay, which are precisely those that
they cost less resources than they benefit
.

Venezuela is a country of unprecedented possibilities, which, despite sitting on huge reserves of oil, lacks it; however, this also applies to ordinary water, as the state's infrastructure is failing, which the government has addressed in an emergency
ingenious regulation of the price of bottled water

The extremely diverse range of things that are in short supply in Venezuela includes, among others, electricity; this is also the problem Maduro is trying to solve - after his last strategy, which consisted of his request to Venezuelan women to stop blow-drying their hair (seriously), and the fiasco with turning off the electricity for four hours a day throughout the country, didn't work, he comes up with a completely new trick: to limit the working and opening hours of various institutions (to save electricity), because he just can't help it anymore. Or would...? Well, the problem is that central planning not only just doesn't work, but

And I ask, what exactly is the crap that society shouldn't tolerate? The man of the Pelican

title_en: ČSSD versus laws; economic and state
text_en:
Lawyer Zdeněk Altner, currently wanted by uniformed monkeys, represented the ČSSD almost twenty years ago in the dispute over the People's House; ČSSD promised him a pretty hefty sum for it, of which, however, it paid only a part, seventeen mega was missing. The legal tussle for the reward lasted for sixteen years, during which it grew thanks to - this is not a classic confusion of the words "thanks" and "due to" - the contractual fine to an incredible 337 million, which is a huge mess for the ČSSD (for that amount, the party could organize three large, massive election campaigns); I am amused by how quickly the leaders of the ČSSD understood the economic laws, which they have stubbornly rejected for a long time in connection with their governance - they have no money, so they lay off people, reduce their working hours and save. That it would open their eyes? No matter what, the socialists can be calm, no one else's blood flows, so they will manage our money in the same way as before.
However, it is not the only thing that politicians in the ČSSD understood; they also found out how much the law sucks... that is, as far as they are concerned. So they refused to pay the money, because they want to take the whole matter to the constitutional court; however, the catch is that this step from the point of view of law does not have a suspensive effect on the court decision, which sounds clear (ČSSD has to pay 337 million) and there is no appeal against it. So the Prime Minister stood before the nation and said that the law sucks; not exactly in those words, but the message was there. Why? Well, Altner is said to be a well-known company, moreover, he is up to his ears in debt, so if the money is sent directly to his account in Switzerland, the debtors may not see anything of it; can i hear well Doesn't the ČSSD accidentally tell us between the lines that when the state court makes an idiotic decision, we are supposed to take the piss out of its decision and "correct" it as we see fit? If that's really the case, then I will once again exceptionally agree on something with those socans.

title_en: Why does Hampl the rat leave the sinking ship?
text_en:

Do you wonder why the snake started a campaign to find out the shape of the Central Bohemian region from day to day, and flew out of the BPI presidency like soapy lightning, which he trumpeted to the media just a few hours after he first introduced it to his closest colleagues? Well, I have an idea. Someone I trust gave me very interesting internal (and so far classified) information from Úsvit, which was supposed to massively finance the Bloc's campaign against Islam: Úsvit was supposedly (again) tunnelled; the account, where there should be 60 million, now allegedly has 59 thousand crowns. This information cannot yet be verified, because if it is true, the party is scrupulously keeping it secret; however, I believe the person who informed me, it all makes perfect sense to me – Hampl has discovered the state of affairs and is leaving the sinking ship before it collapses. Well, those who base their success on populism and collective guilt cannot be surprised that they are surrounded by stupid goons and thieves.

The Ministry of Transport is again buzzing boaters because
apparently it wasn't enough last time
; according to the new decree, not only life jackets will be mandatory, but at the beginning of the season, depending on the weather, gloves, raincoats and beanies (dude...). But that's not all, the rafts must also have a fireman on board in addition to lighting and a lifebuoy (!); however, the crux is the fifteen meter rope - because the ideal thing you most care about when you're snapping and trying to rescue things from the water is getting tangled up in the rope; fifteen meters! But even if the proposal didn't contain any crap or potentially dangerous things, I wonder what business a Ťok has to decide what gear I take with me on the water? The worst thing is that, for example, the mandatory vests are (at least judging by the comments on the Internet) accepted quite positively... why!? Whoever wants a waistcoat, no one prevents him from taking it; but why force it even on those who don't want it? Please, people, think!

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs has invented that abroad the Czech Republic will be translated as Czechia; and we have something to deal with again. Some people like it, others don't, discussions and arguments arise on the given topic, but... it doesn't really matter? Even if the country were to be called Shittia, nothing would really change; I don't understand how anyone can deal with such crap other than critically or for fun. Only if it doesn't have anything to do with
patriotism
, which teaches us
to be proud of things we did not deserve and to hate people we never met
; and in this case still have to solve the problems. I wonder how much the change cost and will cost in terms of salaries of officials or politicians and the price of all other actions associated with it; for example, I personally would not mind at all if the Czech Republic completely disappeared and became part of some other state - and if it brought lower taxes and less state interference, I would certainly applaud it.

title_en: The hand washes the hand, the judge covers the fool
text_en:
A uniformed monkey named Karel Kadlec got drunk last year and crashed two cars with 1.45 percent of alcohol in his blood; At the time, the court dismissed it, stating that it was a misdemeanor, not a crime (it is interesting that here it was also taken into account that the bengs who intervened "did not appear to be under the influence"). Last week, the same drunken pig (he refused a breathalyzer test, then the hospital showed a blood level of over a million) had fun driving his jeep into parked cars, smashing over fifty of them; and because he was a bomber to the end, he didn't even have liability insurance. What will the court say about it this time? Perhaps he will take into account the fact that the person in question taught at the police academy (which, by the way, is also funny) and it will be just a misdemeanor; something like when the
a uniformed chimpanzee who took down a biker
and subsequently kicked the injured person on the ground, according to the judge, he was already sufficiently punished by having to appear in court.
It's basically stolen from me how Kadlec will be punished (but he did mega damage, so in my opinion he should be
