Probably every boater has noticed that, although some dangerous weirs are marked with a no-floating sign, there is almost no floating sign; therefore, most weirs are not marked in any way, which for many years meant that the law did not prohibit floating. However, the Ministry of Transport
it's going to hell
,
redefines brands
and Minister Ťok behaves as if he is off the chain, so their next demented decree prohibits the floating of unmarked weirs; this creates a paradoxical situation where, for example, a weir with a sluice (a channel intended for navigation) cannot be legally crossed if there is no sign (although the very existence of the sluice speaks for itself). And the fine? Well, up to two hundred thousand crowns; yes, you read that right, Ťok has gone completely crazy. For all the so-called "right-wing" ANO voters, I just add that they can congratulate themselves on the election of such an individual (and of course it's not just about weirs, the Ministry of Transport has been kicking it up a notch lately).
What are the likely practical consequences? Those who have moved among boaters can certainly imagine that the majority of them will not even register this decree and the remaining minority will typically ignore it; and that the police would build fences at the dams? I'm not ruling it out, but I'm not assuming either. The biggest problem will be the leaders of children's boating groups, who, for peace of mind, will most likely call the dam managers (if they can get contacts) and request an individual permit (which the law has always allowed); anyway, it will just be another springboard for everyone involved, which Ťok has as much up his ass as he can have. And the reason for all this? Well, most likely the implementation of the good old "ordnung muss sein" to Czech conditions; or the official simply needed to report activity; or some benga really ordered it to be able to cash out (I doubt it, but who knows); or... the state, government, officials, Ťoku, do you know what you can do for me?

The German government gave its goons the green light to use malware (viruses, trojan horses) to track suspects; so, apart from many other pests, the biggest one - that is, the state - will start to spread this crap over our networks. And when I say "us", I'm referring to the fact that the Internet knows no national borders; that the government has legalized actions for which it punishes others is nothing new in the world (wars, taxes, propaganda in schools and the imprisonment of those who do not obey), so I don't want to dwell on it that far, because I find the technical implementation of the whole thing more interesting. Because how does malware spread? Well, viruses can replicate themselves and spread through, for example, various files, worms do so over the network; trojans are programs with some declared functionality (for example, a screen saver, but not limited to that) that the user downloads for himself, but they secretly do something else (for example, play tricks on the government).
So the logical question is how will government malware locate its target; Do they infect fake clouds of computers before they get the real one? After all, we can trust them not to misuse the data obtained from other machines, right? And when this kind of fiddling becomes the norm, will antivirus manufacturers be accused of obstructing the investigation? And no, it's not meant entirely ironically considering that
Apple was already forced by the US government to implement a backdoor in iOS
for the FBI and ISPs are also required to snoop on a court order, just as the owners of various servers are forced to provide snoopers with their user data; is there any reason why it should be any different in the context of anti-state malware fighters? I personally don't see any... so I ask myself when and where will it end? But in addition to asking, I also give
some advice
in conclusion...

Who knows best what is best for children? Their parents? But anyway, that's a long-ago idea; the Ministry of Education will best take care of our children (for our money). And of course, Minister Kateřina Valachová knows this best, because she decided to implement the inclusion of disabled children; the social engineer in question decided that too many pupils were going to special schools, so she and her officials came up with a "solution" (to a problem of her own making): A school counseling facility recommends to individual disabled children whether they should attend a regular school or a special one; if the parents decide to send their child to a standard school, even if he was recommended a special one, everything is fine, but the opposite is no longer the case - whoever sends his child to a special school despite the recommendation of the license plate number, the social worker can boo him to his heart's content, in extreme cases until the children are taken away completely.
Even the well-worn - and completely demented - argument that parents are not "experts" in education, while some civil servants have the paper to do so, can no longer be used here; social workers do not have to be (and typically are not) experts in special pedagogy, so it makes no sense at all. The whole measure is nothing but the unbridled will of the state, which no longer has any inhibitions at all, and whose politicians, officials, bureaucrats and all the other instigators now consider it completely normal that they can decide on whatever they like; some motherfucker from the ministry just makes up her mind and another willing motherfucker from the socialite does not hesitate to destroy families just to satisfy her whims. Don't get mad at me, but this is just so close; and I don't care if the person in question is completely stupid and means well, or if she is simply bored or needs to show activity -
the consequences tend to be dire
in any case.

It was not. Behind nine mountains and nine rivers in the town of Sonnino in Italy, the land of the best cars, lived an absolute madman who didn't like how his wife (didn't) take care of the household and his family; and because he was an extra mean whiner, he was going to turn her in to the fiddler's shop. There were uniformed monkeys sitting in the gymnasium who weren't able to drive their service Alphas, so they were probably bored, which is why they didn't send the bonzak to the proper limits, but instead charged his wife with "domestic abuse", for which she faces two to six years behind bars; whether the court finds her guilty or not (probably not), she will at least be inconvenienced by having to show up and deal with it. And for what!? That she didn't clean, cook and fuck? Seriously? Where are we?
The Italian media accuse the whole case of being sexist because we have equality between the sexes and taking care of the household does not have to be exclusively a woman's job; but is this really the focus of the problem? Is it really an absurd idea today that it would work in every household as its members agree without having a tax-paid arbiter at their disposal? Does the state really have to intervene even in – literally – washing dirty laundry? And if someone is relieved that the incident did not take place in the Czech Republic, don't be too happy - according to the new Civil Code, it is illegal to hide affairs from your partner; a 40-year-old woman from Pardubice is already suing her husband on this topic - she found his mistress and the state is now supposed to force him to provide detailed information about her, including their joint plans. In connection with this, I ask: Who can wipe his ass without the assistance of the state? And who doesn't?

Many supermarkets in France have been honoring such a custom for years: The food they don't sell, they give it to people for free in the evening to take apart; it's usually nothing fresh, but homeless people (or poor Czech students xD) won't look down on it, and supermarkets will save some money on hauling away and getting rid of leftovers. Some time ago I received information that the French parliamentarians are trying to eliminate this custom (due to some hygiene standards), but in practice they probably did not succeed; and because the state simply can't let anything go, everything must be banned, or at least ordered, now it has imposed on French supermarkets the obligation to donate all the food that they would otherwise throw away or give away to charities (transportation costs apparently fall on the donor). President Hollande is so enthusiastic about the regulation that he wants to apply it to restaurants and canteens as well; also pressures Juncker to introduce it in the entire EU, i.e., of course, including the Czech Republic.
Why is this completely wrong? Well, firstly because property rights should be inviolable; it's simply not moral to force someone to give something to someone if they don't want to - after all, how would the supporters of that law like it if they had to obligatorily sort their garbage and transport some of it somewhere at their own expense? This is said to solve the problem of supermarkets wasting food; but what increases their motivation to waste? Yes, that's right, subsidies artificially reduced the purchase price of food; how about stop subsidizing farmers and give space to the market? A frequent criticism of food waste also completely ignores the costs (such as transport) that must be incurred in order to make use of this food; however, these costs (among other things due to pointless subsidies) are often higher than the cost of wasted food. However, it is best to limit waste
free market
, as there is no better way to allocate resources;
every deformation of it
is the road to hell.

title_en: Equality, even if there was no bread
text_en:
Socan Jiří Dienstbier, the minister without portfolio (but she is an official), who is in charge of human rights and equal opportunities, found that only thirteen percent of the 250 companies with the largest turnover in the Czech Republic have women in their management; since the person in question is a social engineer to the core, he decided that wasn't enough - and how did he find that out? Well, instead of humbly accepting that those most unsuccessful in the market, on which by the way Dienstbier
parasitism
, they probably know what they are doing, he decided he knows better than they do; thirteen percent is simply not enough because the parasite politician says it is not enough. According to his own words, it is not about favoring women or men who are of lower quality, but about setting so-called fair rules that will enable both women and men to succeed in such selection procedures. Why is this complete nonsense?
This whole idea is based on the assumption that the most successful companies are not able to select people for their management so well,
as Dienstbier would do
, who himself does not create any values for which people would pay him voluntarily, but uses the state to parasitize those who create;
Maybe those companies didn't choose the best people
, which could? For a long time no one prevented women from pursuing a career, but in our society we have more families where the man earns while the woman takes care of the household than families where it is the other way around; it is not relevant why this is so - it could be tradition, genetic predispositions, whatever - however it follows logically that there are more men (than women) willing to devote their whole lives to a working career, ergo more of them will succeed. Trying to use state violence to force companies to choose other people for their management, before they decide for themselves, only
reduces their effectiveness
and deforms
the market
.

title_en: The Ministry of Transport is going through hell
text_en:
It has not been that long since Minister Ťok and his followers
they redefined the entry ban for trucks
; and they are already sticking out their horns again with proposals for other elements of road buzzing. First of all, it's about allowing the uniformed monkeys to confiscate technicians on the spot if they find too flat tires, a broken exhaust, a broken windshield, body dents, damaged wheels, worn brake pads, and loads of other stuff; and since the authority in a given case has the main say, which is both the prosecutor and the judge, the driver can only complain in retrospect, but at the given moment he finds himself without a car, this is a wonderful buzzer tool of police coercion: "No administrative proceedings, pay the fine on the spot, or..." And how correctly
says D-FENS
: "As soon as a policeman, constable, or official is given any power, he immediately abuses it, and uses it utterly unreasonably whenever and wherever he can and will."
Furthermore, the "two times and enough" or "three times and enough" systems are introduced, which consist in an absolutely absurd increase in points for various offenses; fines are increasing again (not that we don't already have them in relation to the average salary several times higher than in Germany, Austria and most other European countries): driving without a seat belt 1500 (I don't understand why this is an offense at all), for speeding up to 25 thousand (while it is irrelevant what car you have; as if it is equally dangerous in all of them), driving under the influence will be taxed up to 75 thousand (even if there is no accident), as well as driving without a license (the law that we need a permit from the state to drive motor vehicles,
is itself set on its head
) and many others. And it is already traditionally true that once such laws are passed, no one will ever cancel them, at most they will tighten them again; not that it would be of any use, that is, except to clarify who is the master here and who is the pooch.

title_en: Apple to the US government: Shit!
text_en:
Well, for diplomatic reasons, it wasn't straight up shit, but something along the lines of "We have no sympathy for terrorists, we respect FBI professionals, the government has good intentions, we'll cooperate... but we won't give them access to iOS." But let's start from the beginning: A married couple consisting of a terrorist and a terrorist attacked a center for the disabled in San Bernardino a few months ago; both were subsequently shot dead, so the motive remains unclear, as does any possible connection to other terrorists. The only usable trail is their iPhones, so the FBI began pulling various intelligences and, above all, data from Apple; they first cooperated, giving them pretty much everything they had, however it wasn't enough for the geeks, not to mention that there was much more to be gained from the situation, which led to a court ruling that Apple should write an iOS update with a backdoor for the FBI.
However, Tim Cook, the company's CEO, refused; explains the reasons to customers in
an open letter
. He has my respect for this step – as does anyone who stands up to the government; here, it is also positive that Apple is not a shill that the state sweeps away like nothing. The question is, what happens now? How will the court deal with this? It will levy a fine that Apple will have to pay as long as it does not bow to the will of the powers that be, similar to what happened in the case of
Larry Flynt
? Or will it all fade over time? From Tim Cook's reaction, I think that Apple intends to stand by its decision, otherwise, instead of writing flashy open letters, it would leave the backdoor open; and since the person in question is certainly no idiot, and has armies of lawyers and people in the know, whom he must have consulted, but still insists on, I'd say there must be some real chance of success. What do you think?

title_en: Quod licet Iovi, non licet bovi
text_en:
Member of Parliament Štěpán Stupčuk, a member of the road-busting party of the strong-arm ČSSD, drank himself and crashed into a barrier or a sign on D7; when the benga arrived at the scene, the person in question informed them that although he was there alone by the wrecked car, he was not driving, moreover, even though he was completely covered in metal from the looks of it, he couldn't breathe either. Although there are witnesses who say he was driving, the police are now investigating the case; one of the bonkers was even there and offered testimony to the uniformed monkeys that the deputy was indeed driving, however they told him to be careful what he said and what he might get into, they allegedly refused his business card.
To be honest, I don't really care if Stupčok is punished, it would be a steal for me even if he killed himself there, but if he didn't do anything to anyone, he just damaged the infrastructure, in principle there probably wouldn't be anything against anything if the whole matter remained between him, his insurance company and the one who will repair the damage; what bothers me about the whole thing is that exactly these goons from the Social Democracy are one of the first to install laws enabling police traffic jamming (starting with the points system). They are the ones who call the use of a constitutional right "an excuse for a person close to you", call for tougher punishments specifically for drunk drivers, and invent laws that allow the police to bust decent drivers; and why? Well, because those in question invent laws "for the others"; when it concerns them personally, they make exactly what they otherwise call "excuses".

title_en: Another police whip on decent people
text_en:
The Ministry of Transport has redefined the "No Truck Entry" label; it no longer applies only to vehicles over three and a half tons, but now also to light vans, pickups or station wagons with a partition. From the clouds of quite logical restrictions, which were typically the restriction of the entry of excessively heavy cars to the infrastructure, which is not intended for this, with the stroke of an official's pen became a beautiful buzzing instrument, the dream of every uniformed monkey. In addition to bans on entering certain areas, this also applies to faster lanes on some roads where overtaking of trucks is still prohibited; now, even those who have a normal station wagon with a cargo space separated by a grid are not allowed to overtake there, which of course makes a lot of sense, because such a grid in the interior will do wonders for the driving characteristics of any car!
The Ministry of Transport no longer even pretends that the signs should be beneficial, because if they were, it can hardly just redefine their meaning and declare that wherever it was until now "correct" not to allow vehicles over three and a half tons, today even lighter ones are not allowed, depending on how they have separate personal space from cargo space; the real purpose of such nonsense is police buzz and the issuing of fines for actions that do no harm to anyone -
clouds of pointless signs are scattered across the Czech Republic
(especially some completely demented traffic lights, for example in Kralupy I drive past one every week whose contribution to safety is negative, so drivers tend to ignore it, which is why monkeys in uniforms are constantly patrolling there and cashiers), but they will of course welcome any other benga to be able to defend their numbers (in the concentration of scumbags - one per 250 people - the Czech Republic is one of the world's best, only a few totalitarian regimes compete with it).

Babiš's henchman Martin Stropnický went to the elections for the ANO movement with a billboard proclaiming: "So that children are not ashamed of us," which received
funny dimension
at the moment when his son Matěj Stropnický, who is making a career with the Greens, who reproached him for being elected to the Prague council only thanks to the support of his father and his master Babiš, now needed to score points with the Greens, so he labeled the ANO movement (from which he received support before the elections, for which he did not hesitate to ask Babiš himself personally and through his father) as a fraud and its members as people incapable of independent thinking, who simply cannot do anything; Martin Stropnický refused to comment on these statements, but I would say that there must be mutual pride between father and son, because they both behave like real politicians - pandering, cronyism, betrayal, without comment - with their value rankings, they must be puffing with pride.
And since the Greens are a similar group, this move worked out without a hitch, they elected Stropnický junior as chairman, after all, he is now known in the media for his statements, so what more could you want; just by the way, a family has not only a father and a son, but also
mom in politics
, how touching. Anyway, while Martin Stropnický seconded his master and ruler Babiš, Matěj Stropnický ran into
Havel's rhetoric
, so in his last interview as the chairman of the Greens, he stated that he was against motoring, but just a few minutes later also that it is not normal for eighty percent of the citizens of the Czech Republic to be able to afford an air vacation, which was preceded by the statement that he himself flies; however, the plebs should most likely be transported by bicycle and train. The whole thing would be laughable if it weren't for crying; why? Because people
both choose
; and i ask
why should i follow the law
, which produce such a spineless beast?

For about a week now, I've been working on nothing but VAT control reports for our Czech customers; in addition to me, there is another programmer, financial analyst and designer flying around - the price of the work of the four of us just for a week for those few companies is about two hundred thousand crowns wasted because of the state because we extinguish their problems with control reports (most of our customers are abroad, where Babišova does not have much reach). Every time something like this is introduced we hear political bullshit about how it will all go smoothly and there will be no problems and almost no cost; I always remember that when I solve the problems - not exactly cheap. Well, I just started the compilation, in the meantime I opened the news on the Internet... and lo and behold, comrades Babiš and Sobotka silenced the opposition obstructionists and introduced us to EET; I can already see how everything will be technically completely trouble-free again.
In addition to the introduction of EET on the side of those who provide the information, another "fun" will be the introduction of EET on the side of the state that will receive the data; the Ministry of Finance initially tried to keep the project specification a secret (for some reason), but when its full, uncensored version began to circulate on the Internet (for example, from
my storage
it's been downloadable for a few months now), published by them too (google "EET specs"). Anyone who has at least some knowledge of information systems can have fun (even if it's quite dark humor),
the project is absolutely pathetic
; but what else can we expect from the state? Although the technical side is understandably the less important part of the whole thing, about the moral aspect of EET
I have already written enough
; now that the law has passed (the opposition is said to be going to challenge it in the constitutional court, which I don't give too much of a chance), it will be interesting to see how the incompetent state gets this system going.

title_en: The Ministry of Health reports activity
text_en:
Svatopluk Němeček and his melody boys from the Ministry of Health need to shine once again and show their activity, because since their totalitarian ban on smoking in private pubs they haven't really been heard of; how else can you explain the completely demented law they came up with now? First, alcohol may not be sold at children's events; mind you, not that it shouldn't be sold to children (although that too), but it shouldn't be sold there at all, not even to parents. Second, the sale of beverages containing more than four percent ethanol should be prohibited at sporting events; ten yes, twelve no more, forget about the welder and even more so about anything harder. And the reason? Well, that's a question! I honestly can't think of any reasonable ones; after all, the state does not even officially seek to prevent alcohol (in general) from being sold, so why these exceptions?
It is nothing but inventing laws for the sake of laws, reporting activity for activity, real benefits nowhere, something is simply banned because nothing has been banned for a "long time"; unfortunately, this is also how totality comes to us - it's not just the devil Babiš and his well-thought-out plans, it's also the bored comrade Němeček and his need to do something simply because "it's his job" and that's how it's expected of him. Clouds of people - stupid democracies - even applaud it in the style that they don't like alcohol, parents don't have to drink at their children's events and they don't do it themselves, so why not ban it, right? Their opponents typically argue that drinking beer is not a bad thing. Someone who deals with the essentials, i.e. not drinking or not drinking, but state prohibitions, which in practice mean absolutely inexcusable threats of physical violence to sellers, to make people look... it makes me sad.

A thirteen-year-old German girl with Russian roots didn't come to school one day, then didn't even come home, and didn't show up until the next day; and then when she finally returned, she claimed she was raped by African refugees. The Russian foreign minister made a fuss that the German media allegedly tried to cover up the case; but the Internet is powerful, so it got out anyway, the Islamobes held demonstrations, stirred up emotions, and people with political ambitions warmed their lips a little. After a few days, however, the girl reportedly changed her statement and admitted that she ran away because of problems at school and the sex was allegedly voluntary; the reactions of the public are quite typical: the Sunniks attack the Islam killers for spreading hoaxes, while many of them are convinced that the girl was really raped and that the change in the statement is just a cover version, because the police processed the person in question, because raping refugees do not fit into the media image of political correctness.
In this text, I don't want to decide where the truth is - I do apply George Carlin's first rule: "I don't believe anything the government tells me," but this does not mean that I should blindly believe the opposite, so in principle I admit that the truth can be both (although after a thorough study of the available information, one of the versions seems more likely to me); however, the public's reactions to this case are much more interesting: I have read the opinions of dozens of Islamo-killers who "know for sure" that the woman in question was raped; but also the opinions of many sun lovers, they already "know" that she made it up. The catch is that from the information available, neither can be said with certainty; and the sad thing is how a huge number of people do this just because it fits their worldview - unfortunately most debates on this topic show that there is no logic or arguments at all anymore, because discussions about migration are already conducted almost exclusively emotionally.

We all probably know the magic trick of the former mayor of Prague, Pavel Bém: "I'll make seven hundred million disappear and guess which card you're thinking of." A few years have passed since then, and to the already brutal purchase price (less than three quarters of a billion), another more than a billion was added for operation. And remember that crap about how it's going to be a multi-functional card that can be used everywhere? Well, "surprise," that was a lie; in practice it is a tram for almost two gigabytes. What did not happen, however, was that the political leadership of Prague changed, so a new card called Lítačka enters the scene; on the one hand, it costs ten million, on the other, of course, the question is how it will work (not that there are no problems with Opencard). In any case, it is remarkable how the same service can be obtained two orders of magnitude cheaper; imagine that in life you are deciding whether to pay ten thousand or a kilo for something... such a common situation, right?
This whole affair shows the absurdity of the management of public funds in so many ways as to be ridiculous; for example: Mass transport is subsidized, individual transport is taxed, yet politicians constantly solve the problem of "too many cars" - what does this say about the quality of public transport? There is a project that can be purchased for billions, but also for tens of millions; what will be the difference in quality? Even if there was one, has anyone asked the people of the city of Prague which option they prefer? Why do some have to pay for the transport of others? For what reason does DPP have to be subsidized by ten billion annually from public budgets, although it practically has a monopoly on public transport in a city of more than a million people? Who is responsible for this limitless waste? How would the managers of a private company who managed in this way fare?

The master of scumbags Babiš and his slimy scumbag padawan Sobotka eat hell together; their government approved another law "against tax evasion" - the CNB will introduce a central database of accounts of legal and natural persons and financial movements on these accounts. Benga, Bernák, the secret services and of course Babiš's Ministry of Finance will have free access to the information (which is updated daily, by the way), which is certainly not a conflict of interest, because Babiš would understandably never abuse it, because he already has enough money, so he doesn't need anything like that; Babiš himself says that in this way he intends to minimize the risk of information leakage in sensitive cases - completely logically, because the database will be state-owned, so it cannot be hacked, and the scammers will also be state-owned, so it will be honest, fair, virtuous and discreet, so no one will ever think of abusing this register, because it is not at all one of the most attractive information systems that the state has ever had.
And since we already have a law from above limiting the amount of payment in cash, it will definitely be possible to bend it further and tighten it; the right to "have an account" has already been recognized by the EU, so it is only a matter of time before it becomes an obligation, which is only a step away from the ban on cash payments and the transfer of all legal transactions to Babiš's database. The advantage is that introducing something like this in the Czech Republic without other countries doing it is probably not politically feasible enough; the disadvantage is that when they do it, the argument will come again: "It works in developed Western countries, so we must have it too."
The government will ban Bitcoin as the currency of pedophiles and mafias
at the moment when it gains a little popularity, like all other alternative currencies, they can then be liquidated as a means of bypassing the CNB account register, since these will then be taken as
a given without which the world simply could not function
and doom would ensue; how about it worked for thousands of years?

Today we look at Denmark again - in Sonderborg, a 17-year-old girl was attacked by a sexual assailant (media reports say it was a foreigner, some suggest it was an asylum seeker; given today's political correctness, I think it's likely that it was, they just don't want to write it in full), knocked her to the ground and started taking off her pants; the person in question has my respect twice – firstly she defended herself and secondly she did so with pepper spray, the possession of which is illegal in Denmark. I'd consider it an adequate defense if she pulled out a quiver and shot him with balls, but if she did, she'd be in even more trouble than she is now; yes, you read that right, the person in question has a problem. Danish police spokesman Knud Kirsten reported that the person was charged with illegal weapons; what kind of stomach does a person have to announce this to the public and continue to work on behalf of the criminal organization that punishes the victims?
What's sad about the whole thing (besides the fact that it happened at all) is the reaction of people, many of whom are calling for more police and a tougher approach to immigrants; how does that make sense in the context of this case? After all, the person in question defended herself! Of course, the attacker can do it again, but he couldn't if the girl had used a deadly weapon instead of a pepper spray; the police do not deal with such a thing, because they either lock him up (at the taxpayers' expense) and release him again, or deport him, which will prevent him from raping again in Denmark, but not elsewhere. State repression has never been as effective in the fight against crime (which is often committed by state forces) as an armed society; the attacker's fear of an armed victim also works as a prevention (not to mention that armed victims reduce the number of attackers over time). However, due to massive state propaganda, this obvious logic is not available to most people.

The Ministry of Education proposed a decree that specifies the foods that may be sold (even in vending machines) in schools (the list of what is prohibited was no longer enough here, now we have a list of what is allowed and everything else may not be sold); this regulation is so harsh that even fruit yogurts, milks, creams (not to mention sweet lemonades, baguettes, chips and the like) do not pass. The dobrosers' idea of the practical impact of the decree is that children will eat healthier; and to some extent this is no doubt true... but what will the other effects be? Well, when we ran out of baguettes in the school vending machine, we went to the store across the street to buy them (it's true, not all of them, but a significant part); therefore, in addition to the intended impact, the decree gives students one more reason to leave school during breaks... will we solve the increase in traffic accidents in the vicinity of schools in a few years? And who will associate it with the regulation of vending machines and buffets?
Far more interesting, however, is the widespread support of similar initiatives by the public (the lobby to ban the sale of junk food in schools has existed for years; and when I occasionally spoke against them in some discussion, it always caused a huge wave of resentment); not that I don't understand parents' efforts to provide their children with healthy food, but... is this really the right way? How about putting that energy into raising children? Quite possibly then these children would not even have the need to stuff themselves with chips outside of school. And if you're going to ban something, why not go to the school principal (who can decide what's sold in the school) and convince him? It is also noteworthy that local bans of this type were at an absolute minimum, because no one really cared about them; however, as soon as it comes to a blanket ban on something by law and further restrictions on freedoms (even "private" schools), everyone is immediately enthusiastic, full of support and energy... do you really think that we are banning ourselves to a better world?

Babiš has already proven to us many times that he will do anything to achieve his goals; walking over the corpses of our various freedoms is nothing unusual, most politicians do that, but unlike them, the owner of Agrofert has no problem letting himself go for his campaign
take a picture while excreting
. He is also able to accept refugees once, only to come out harshly against them after a few months, when he found that it could get him some votes; when promoting the EET, he did not hesitate to limit the right of the opposition to comment on the proposal, which did reduce his popularity a little, but he has a great remedy for this: He will reduce the VAT on beer! Is there any better way to fuck the Czechs? Of course, I have nothing against reducing VAT (even if only for one item), I'm just pointing out its motivation.
On a related note, I'd like to post some behind-the-scenes information that has come my way; I have no guarantee that this is true, nor have I confirmed anything from two independent sources, I am only relaying what I have learned: Babiš is said to be buying a majority stake in Ahold (Albert, Interspar, Hypernova), which would make him the owner of the largest retail chain in the Czech Republic, which plans to supply Agrofert. How does this relate to EET? Well, if Babiš used information from the Ministry of Finance when buying competitors and other companies, with which a potential seller can blackmail, EET would bring him supplies of additional ammunition for similar practices (businessmen would not have to be punished by the state for tax evasion, but by Agrofert). I don't have any evidence for such a claim, nor do I know for sure if it's true, but I trust my source more than Babiš (well, probably everyone) and it definitely makes sense to me.

Oxfam, which constantly supplies us with studies on the topic of how much of the world's wealth is owned by what percentage of people, has come up with the fact that a long-daunted line has been crossed: The richest one percent now own more than the rest of the world. They added a call for politicians to fight it. Oxfam's conclusions were opposed by economists from the Deloitte Group; as? Well, they challenged the methodology that defines a person's wealth as the value of assets minus the value of debt, which makes a fifth of Americans and Europeans living on welfare and with, say, student loans, poorer people than starving children in Africa who are on zero; in addition, they acknowledge that wealth inequality is too high and "something needs to be done about it".
That's what I call argumentative bullshit: getting bogged down in details and approving demented conclusions. So what is the main problem with such studies? First of all, the constant emphasis on inequality in ratio and total ignorance of the fact that
absolute wealth continues to increase at a rapid rate
; even the poor get rich, so what about the rich getting richer faster? It is constantly presented as if the rich are getting richer at the expense of the poor; in fact, it is a reciprocal process (someone produces something, thereby becoming very rich; but also everyone who buys from him raises his standard a little). Furthermore, it is forgotten that the groups of "rich" and "poor" are not constant, but people migrate between them (so it is not always the same individuals). But most importantly: Taxation may reduce relative wealth differences, but
the overall growth of wealth is clearly inhibited by redistribution
!
So what might help today's poor, harms tomorrow's.

Imagine an organized group that works by scouting out a rich businessman, liquidating him and disposing of his assets; what doesn't suit them, they simply auction it off. Reprehensible, isn't it? Would you buy from them? Now imagine living in a society where something like this happens quite openly and openly; wouldn't that be bad? Well, I have bad news for you: You live in such a society. Benga hit a Chomut drug maker, jailed him and took his cars (Ferraris, Hummers and some others) which are now up for auction; since they had no luck shooting hummers for 850k last time, now they're trying again for half meg. Everything takes place in public, the actors are clearly not ashamed of their actions, on the contrary, they even brag about it; and most people don't even blink, they don't find anything objectionable about it.
Why? Because it was a drug manufacturer? So what? That he made things that could harm people? Yesterday I wrote about what capitalism is not; and he did not miss the opportunity to refute some of his delusions
critics
. Today I would like to write a few lines about what capitalism is; To begin with, I would like to quote a man whom I consider to be the greatest thinker of the twentieth century and probably of all time - Murray Newton Rothbard:
Capitalism is the fullest expression of anarchism; anarchism is the fullest expression of capitalism. The true anarchism will be capitalism; and the true capitalism will be anarchism.
If by chance someone longed for a translation, then a capitalist creation
Google Translate handles it quite well
(with narrowed eyes).
So what does the term capitalism mean? It is a free market in which the state does not interfere. Yes, sure, capitalists can be ruthless entrepreneurs motivated by their own selfishness and greed, which is a big problem in conjunction with the state - corruption, laws tailored to their companies, subsidies, monopolies (which by the way
they do not arise without the state
); however, in a free market environment, the same profiteering and avarice lead those same people to satisfy the needs of others - how else can they get money without the state, other than by convincing people to use their services and buy their products?
And what is the best way to convince someone to buy something from you? Of course, in the way that you offer him the thing that the person needs! Maybe some people think that this is a beautiful theory, but in practice it works completely differently; yes, of course, you are right, it works differently in practice, but why? Well, because of the state, of course. In the free market, it really works just as I describe; just look at places where the state doesn't interfere so much - Singapore, Hong Kong and others - how are they flourishing? But what about socialist Sweden? Isn't there another way? No; just look at the history, Sweden got its wealth in the days of wild capitalism, socialism was installed only after the country was extremely rich (and this growth was also significantly retarded).
Capitalism is freedom and abundance; capitalism means the free market, which has taken us from carriages to cars, from typewriters to computers, from empty pantries to full refrigerators, from toil in the fields to the possibility of choosing a career in countless fields, from the huge price of food to the negligible, from the occasional wash in the stream to luxurious bathrooms, from one outfit per person to full closets, from a box to a flush toilet, from days or weeks needed to travel to hours, in short, from poverty to riches! Make no mistake, this is not the work of an official, behind it is still greed, personal gain and the pursuit of mammon... the same qualities that turn the state into a disaster, the market can exploit for our good.

In recent years, I have observed around me that criticism of capitalism is becoming extremely fashionable and popular, especially among young people (but by no means only among them); what about that, let everyone define himself against what he himself deems appropriate. However, I find it very sad and alarming that the vast majority of those who rail against capitalism typically have no idea what capitalism is; and the problem is not that they simply "define it differently", which in itself wouldn't matter if they stick to such definitions consistently, but they, in their majority, criticize a kind of mischief, but they want to restrict real capitalism by law.
First of all, I would like to give a few examples of what capitalism is definitely not: Capitalism is definitely not Agrofert and Babiš, it is the products of socialist subsidies and regulations (biofuels...); capitalism is not private schools absolutely limited by state regulations; capitalism is seriously not private health insurance companies when health insurance is compulsory; capitalism is definitely not even a (non-state) company that the state will grant a monopoly on anything (water supplies, for example). Where there is no free market, there cannot be capitalism; and if the state interferes somewhere, then it is not a free market.
Some people argue that it is not the state's fault that large companies have non-market privileges, but the corporations' fault, because they bribe state officials and politicians; regardless of the outcome of the academic debate on the topic of who is more to blame, it is quite evident how the problem cannot be solved - giving more power to the state. Even if it were perfectly true that it is only the fault of large corporations that paid politicians create laws tailored to them, it cannot be argued that the state will solve it (because the problem arose precisely because it did not); if states are corrupted by big players in the market, then regardless of who is to blame, the consequence of increasing state power can be nothing but more corruption!
You can blame businessmen for corrupting politicians; but as long as there are entrepreneurs in a market environment and politicians with the power to distort this environment, corruption cannot naturally not occur (by the way, the records of it are thousands of years old, obviously it has never been different; nor could it be). Therefore, the only solution is to either take away entrepreneurs the opportunity to do business, or politicians the opportunity to make decisions; and perhaps everyone who either remembers the first version, or at least
theoretically understands
, why it is a road to hell, he should at the same time realize that the problem cannot be solved other than by removing political power (adding it will achieve the opposite). And for those who still don't realize it, I have one of those
picture
...

An incomparably more dangerous group that initiates an order of magnitude more violence than all migrants combined are our nation states and the European Union; not citizens, not ordinary people, not "all of us", no "society", but states, which are politicians, officials, policemen and other parasites living off our money, which they take from us under the threat of violence and call it taxes. These people rob us, impose their will on us, and if we do not submit, they take us by force and lock us up in prison (even if we do not harm anyone; for example, only because we refuse to pay them or do not want to let them interfere with our transactions); they are people who commit more violence every day than immigrants do in a whole year. I'm not saying that mass migration is not a threat, I'm just calling for reflection on whether it's reasonable, as part of the solution to this problem, to strengthen the powers of a state that generates more evil and violence than all immigrants combined.

title_en: Babiš is so rich that he wouldn't steal
text_en:

Of course, I don't mean to imply that someone who is rich is more likely to steal, I'm just pointing out that it doesn't exactly make sense to assume the opposite. Anyway, what does the hard data say? Agrofert's income tax amounted to two billion crowns in 2011, while Agrofert received a little over half a billion in subsidies; and as time went by, the first number fell while the second grew, until finally Agrofert's annual report for 2014 shows that it paid a billion and a half in income tax, while it siphoned off almost a billion and three quarters from subsidies. But that's a coincidence; similar to when, as the Minister of Finance, he forgave the state fees in the amount of one and a half billion.
I am the last person who would mind if someone optimizes taxes and tries to pay as little as possible to the state; however, it is a call to heaven when the one who is making a big fuss about everyone with EET, the VAT control report and pours money into his own pocket from the subsidies that all taxpayers have to pay for does so. In every society, there will be a certain percentage of people of Babiš's type - capable, clever, predatory and ruthless; however, the difference is in how they manifest themselves: While in the free market all those Babišs will be a threat to competition and a benefit to customers (following the example of Rockefeller's Standard Oil), the state opens up a more attractive and easier way for them to build their empires - instead of lowering prices, pandering to customers and eliminating competition, all you have to do is use the state's coercive apparatus and forcibly force everyone to pay.

title_en: Snow White with the Black Man
text_en:
A wave of resentment was raised by Miroslav Donutil's work recently broadcast on ČT - a remake of Snow White, in which the prince was black; so with curiosity I went to listen to the fairy tale and it was really terrible, but the black prince was about the least of my problems in my eyes. Yes, sure, there were some slightly racist innuendos, for example the disadvantages of Snow White's white skin were pointed out, but damn, I'm not too picky about racism personally; however, I was much more struck by the absolute mental (actually also spiritual, but I would forgive that) emptiness of the entire fairy tale – not only the battle of good and evil, but all hardships were omitted, the heroes simply did not face any problems: Snow White found the dwarfs, cooked for them, they dug for gold, she went to the city, met the black prince there, they got married and had children; I'm seriously not exaggerating, absolutely no hint of the slightest plot, overcoming hardships and pitfalls.
This complete toothlessness is not accidental, it is a common feature of many modern fairy tales - mainly not defending yourself, the fight of good against evil is "out", courage or solving problems is like a broom; the main character must not show initiative and influence things that simply flow around him (for example, Harry Potter - something is happening there, but
the main character shows no foresight or effort to take matters into his own hands
, rather the opposite), because we have to protect children from getting the impression that each of us is the engineer, engineer and driver of our own happiness - things just happen that way regardless of our actions. Those who do well are "lucky", otherwise "bad luck" is to blame, especially not the person concerned. The motto of many modern fairy tales is: "He who does nothing, spoils nothing; so above all, don't stand out." How will such stories influence the generation that grows up with them? In comparison, the Black Prince is seriously a completely unproblematic character.

The essence of freedom of speech is that I can say what I want, but no one is obliged to provide me with the means to spread it!

title_en: Murray Newton Rothbard; requiescat in pace
text_en:
Today it is exactly twenty-one years since one of the greatest thinkers, economists, philosophers and geniuses of the twentieth century and, in my opinion, of all time left this world at the age of 69 - Murray Newton Rothbard, the "father of anarcho-capitalism"; the importance of his work lies in the incredibly consistent unification of two seemingly unrelated trends: the Austrian school of economics and anarchism. His teacher, the outstanding economist Ludwig von Mises, proved the impossibility of economic calculation in central planning, thus proving beyond doubt the superiority of the free market economy over the socialist one, he still assumed that the free market would be ensured by the state; on the other hand, various anarchists pointed to the ethical indefensibleness of the state as a monopoly on violence, but their solution was typically various communist utopias lacking economic foundations.
In his life's work, Murray Newton Rothbard consistently combined these two directions into a consistent anarcho-capitalism, because he understood that the obstacle to anarchy and the free market is the state, while the absence of a monopoly on violence means anarchy and a free market, which he expressed as follows: "Capitalism is the fullest expression of anarchism, and anarchism is the fullest expression of capitalism. Not only are they compatible, but you can't really have one without the other. True anarchism will be capitalism, and true capitalism will be anarchism." He was a man of sharp analytical mind with an absolute sense of logic, but at the same time very emotional; an implacable hatred of evil, whose greatest contemporary embodiment is the state, permeated his entire work. He died when I was not yet ten years old; however, later on, what he created greatly influenced my life and opened my eyes. Thank you, Mr. Rothbard.

The Chinese government has started running an app called Sesame Credit (if you google it, beware of being confused with Credit Sesame, which is a different piece of software) whose job it is to find out how good a citizen is and assign people a score based on that; this will subsequently be taken into account during negotiations with the authorities and the state in general, but it may also affect, for example, the availability of loans, the amount of pensions and the like. Registration is not yet mandatory, however the comrades plan that it should be by 2020; according to available information, the goal is for everyone to have an account established at birth and remain with them throughout their lives.
From the sources I've gone through, I haven't been able to figure out exactly how the point system works; rather, the result of my search was finding contradictory information (according to some, the application will monitor practically anything, including activities on social networks - by sharing pro-government materials you gain points, by sharing anti-government materials you lose them; however, the creators of the application deny this). Be that as it may, the introduction of such a system means laying the foundations for absolute totalitarian control; over time, it will seem completely normal to people, similar to, for example, the Czech census has clouds of supporters. And just as Babiš argues when introducing EET that they also have it in Croatia, I wonder if I will live to see the first Czech politician start justifying the introduction of Sesame Credit by saying that it brings great results in China.

Second, I find it remarkable how many people address the victim's mistakes or stupidity while ignoring the aggressor's crap; what if I lock someone up somewhere if they don't obey me? Third, it's interesting how everyone keeps whining about the lack of ideals and admiring romantic heroes who won't stoop to terror, but when someone actually does it, they're an idiot. Not only from libertarians, I occasionally read arguments in the sense of "the worse, the better", which generally reckon that the current establishment (the rotten state, the EU) must soon collapse under its own weight, because what the politicians are presenting is unsustainable; yes, that's right, it's not sustainable, and if socialism continues to grow, over time, it will not only hinder the prosperity of our society, it may even stop it, so we will start to become poorer, which will eventually lead to a fall. But when? It took the Soviet Union almost three generations, and it still had much better conditions to fall than what we have here now. Why? First, it was seriously completely centrally planned, we are only partially so; secondly, the overall level of wealth was then lower, ergo the path to absolute poverty was shorter; thirdly, the degree of personal freedom (words, confession, ...) was lower; fourthly, there was a positive example of "the West" (even if it was not allowed to be talked about).
The power of the market is fascinating; despite all the regulations and the huge ball on the foot in the form of the public sector, the private sector still manages to generate wealth. There is a historical example that tells us that even after this is not the case, it may take three generations for a change to occur; counting the time before we even start to get poor, we are at best talking about our great-great-grandchildren, who might be affected. This is not to say that the EU cannot fall sooner, on the other hand, it will be replaced by another socialism without any problems. That's why I wouldn't get too attached to the motto "the worse the better"; it's another thing to support things that ridicule or divide the establishment, but their real danger is minimal (now, for example, the best Czech clown named Zeman). So what is our only - albeit meager - chance? Let us tirelessly explain to the people the benefits of freedom; here is another year and with it new armies of indoctrinated statists... so we have work xD

title_en: Helping and protecting... and tearing down
text_en:
In 2014 (we don't have this year's statistics yet), 1,327 official vehicles of monkeys and 84,532 cars driven by normal people were involved in traffic accidents; in total, 8,282 monkey cars and 7.8 million human cars were registered at the beginning of the same year. It follows that during the period in question about 1% of humans and 16% of apes were felling, which were supposed to help and protect those humans; can the sixteenfold accident rate be explained by the greater number of kilometers driven? The average human car travels fifteen thousand kilometers a year, the police do not have exact statistics, but in order to balance the above disparity, the apes would have to drive a quarter of a million a year, which would actually mean an annual replacement of the vehicle fleet - and according to the financial reports of the police, this does not even happen by mistake.
Not to mention that even if mileage explained such a huge number of accidents, according to the state's own logic, it does not excuse anyone - or does the point system somehow take into account who drives more kilometers? No. Are points deleted based on accident free kilometers? No. So why should benga be judged by any other standards? They just crash sixteen times more often than others and make a mess on the roads.
One might argue that the uniformed monkeys are involved in so many accidents because they chase criminals and "pirates"; But does chasing give them the right to threaten others? No. Even the state does not give them such a right, because according to the law they can violate the regulations, but only so as not to threaten anyone. Of the 1,327 accidents in which they were involved, they were at fault in 661, and in 666 they were innocent (assuming that their colleagues and the courts do not favor them, which I doubt); therefore, it cannot even be argued that the monkeys are innocent in this and the criminals are breaking into them.
And the lesson? Cops are aggressive, blunt beasts, dangerous to themselves (which is the last thing that would bother me) and to the environment; the state tells us they are on the roads to help and protect us, but in reality they are pests. And when I hear politicians talking about piles of dead on the roads and "pirates", I think they should sweep their own doorsteps first, because the only real pirates are their henchmen.

title_en: Is multiculturalism the root of evil?
text_en:
Especially recently, especially in connection with the migration crisis, we can read from many authors that multiculturalism is evil, it fails, it has never worked and it will lead us to destruction; and I can't disagree that if the politicians keep pushing multiculturalism to us like they have been doing so far, nothing good will really come of it. However, I have a bit of a feeling that among the authors of similar texts there is often a rather fatal misunderstanding of the cause of the real problem, which in my opinion is simply not multiculturalism; it is state-enforced multiculturalism.
What would multiculturalism look like without state support? Well, Rooster-type lunatics would probably continue to go to the ghetto to kiss gypsies, all sorts of left-leaning students would still stuff it for us, write articles about it, and a few of them might even move some refugees into their homes; and I personally guess that with this step some of them would cure themselves of multiculturalism. But what would be the real impact on a normal person? Practically none, we can all ignore the rooster and the numbers of #accepted refugees would most likely be in the units or small tens.
So why is multiculturalism a problem? Because the state imposes it on us under the threat of violence; we don't suffer because of idiots kissing gypsies, but because of anti-discrimination laws, because of mandatory EU refugee quotas, because of expensive detention camps, because of mandatory integration, because of non-profits connected to state money pipes, in short because of politicians and people paid with public money who need to defend their existence. Multiculturalism by itself, without state support, would be nothing more than a fairly harmless pastime for a few coffee shop leftists (and without the connection to public money, there would be even fewer of them).
So we have two problematic factors here: the State and multiculturalism. What would a state do without multiculturalism? Bureaucrats would simply find another excuse to prey on decent people. And what would multiculturalists do without a state? At most, they would arouse sympathetic smiles from those around them. Unfortunately, I therefore come to the same conclusion as I have done so many times - the primary cause of the problem is once again the state; and as many times before, the situation appears different at first glance, so many even see the solution in further state interventions (only on the opposite side), while it would be more than enough if the government gave the people a break.

However, the patriots are more impressed by violence than any language, so they catapulted Mr. Ortel and his Ortel to the heights of the Czech Nightingale vote, which increased his popularity even more.
Speaking of Ortel
also written by D-FENS

I recommend the song "Rag" to the readers because it is a power; just by the way, that gem is also the anthem of the Workers' Party. The biggest pain, however, is the piece "Stay My Home" - I've never heard something so pathetic in my life; I just don't have words for it, you have to hear it (and also see it; the clip highlights all the wretchedness). This song is best described by this quote from George Carlin (I'm not sure if he's the original author): "Nationalism teaches you to take pride in shit you haven't done and hate people you've never met." Unfortunately, doing something in life costs time, energy, resources, effort, while belonging to a nation can be done effortlessly by anyone, so it's easier to be proud of the other; and that is why patriotism is so popular, it is actually the ideal ideology for the desperate.

I've made a few changes to the Stok code, but I've already had a few additional or confused questions about what's going on, so I'll allow myself to briefly comment on them - firstly, I added an RSS feed, there's probably nothing to explain, anyone who uses RSS readers can add my channel; secondly, I've made a few changes regarding the appearance that may not be entirely clear at first glance. Unregistered visitors have it easy, a new item has been added to the menu (» appearance «), where they can choose how Stoky should look for them; the settings will be stored in browser cookies. Registered users have it a bit more complicated; in addition to the »appearance« item, they also have the »change account data« option, where they can choose the same, however, this setting will not be stored in cookies, but in the database of their user accounts.
What is the difference? Whatever you set in the » appearance « menu will be saved only in the browser where you set it; on the other hand, via »change account data«, you can set the form that Stoky will have wherever you log in from. In case of a conflict between the settings, the user "wins" (» change account data «), however there is an option (the very first one) that can reverse it (ie the user's appearance will correspond to what he chose in the menu » appearance «); you can use this to turn off Stok sounds at work (the black-and-white appearance without images is also without sounds), which some readers have asked me to do. And as I just verified the theory in practice, changing the coat of the website is very easy thanks to CSS, so if anyone has an idea or wish in the form of another appearance, do not hesitate to write; if more similar proposals come together, or if I like something, I will implement it.

Although I'm not a big fan of hip hop, I have to ask: Have you ever heard libertarian rap? If not, google it

Unfortunately, these two works perfectly illustrate the current state of individualism and collectivism in society; while libertarian ideas are indeed logical, strongly consistent, complete and true - and no one takes them seriously at all, because their understanding requires a certain effort, collectivist ideas are typically populist inconsistent rants that look good at first glance, but a deeper logical analysis shows their nonsense - and everyone understands them and many even consider them an ideal (the smarter ones sometimes add that it is an unattainable ideal). If we add to this the fact that libertarians are often exotics (like me) for whom the shorthand and imprecise communication so important to populism is a problem, we do have the best goods, but without any advertising, so we don't sell; what about that

I don't celebrate Christmas in the traditional sense of the word (with my family, we typically have a nice day characterized by good food, visits and playing computer games together, but we don't stress about cleaning, sweets, "obligatory" buying of gifts and the like), but as an anarcho-capitalist and a Christian, I think they are God's; why?
Christians were able to use this originally pagan holiday for their PR and turn it into a commemoration of the birth of the Lord Jesus, whom God sent to redeem us from sin and suffer for our sins, for which I personally am infinitely grateful to him (despite the light tone of the whole text, I mean this sentence completely seriously), although apparently he was not even born in winter (all the interesting astronomical phenomena around the year zero, which could be by the Bethlehem Comet, whether it was 1P/Halley or not, they come out to different seasons); libertarians should take a cue from Christians regarding their approach to PR xD
In modern times, moreover, Christmas has become a very consumerist pastime (and I will also make money from this year's holidays, as I will celebrate all the holidays, including today, with a well-paid job), which is very good, so many voluntary shifts will probably never take place at any other time of the year; I make a living, among other things, by programming ERP systems for giant retail and wholesale chains, some of which are able to realize up to 80% (!!) of their annual sales in December. So to people who complain that the spirit of Christmas has been replaced by consumerism, I say: Even the original purpose of Christmas was to celebrate (even those that had nothing to do with Jesus), so don't be smart and enjoy it; and if you lack spirituality, pray - I personally do so not only at Christmas and I can warmly recommend it.

However, if there is still someone among the readers whom I have not infected with the Christmas spirit and convinced them that Christmas is God's (which perhaps everyone must see clearly by now), for that I can lovingly rummage

As one calls to the forest, so one calls from the forest; and this is doubly true of collective guilt: If we divide people into "us" and "them" (according to anything other than the actions of specific individuals) in order to restrict the freedom of "the others" based on how some of "them" have transgressed, we give great arguments to "their" populists who also preach collective guilt; and the more we behave like that, the more "they" will perceive it as well, which will again confirm the words of "our" populists, and everything can escalate to absurdity. If we apply this to refugees, we find that by curtailing their liberties we are seriously driving them into the arms of various terrorist organizations; but watch out! There is no good idea that cannot be twisted and abused; and this, unfortunately, is demonstrated by the sun-lovers: They divide society into "us" and "them" exactly the same, but they limit "our" freedoms in favor of "them" and even brazenly argue that if they don't do so, "they" will become radicalized.
Do you know what the German sunshine politicians are calling for now? They want to ban New Year's Eve fireworks so they don't traumatize the refugees, because the fireworks could remind them of the war; and the curtailment of our freedoms are defended by saying that we must step back so as not to radicalize anyone. But don't they realize that's what they're doing? After all, the principle applies to both sides, and it is completely irrelevant who started it; by restricting the freedoms of the local residents, they will understandably begin to feel threatened and more and more of them will insist on dividing "us" versus "them", which will lead to the same thing on the other side. How is it possible that this principle is well understood by the sun worshipers in one direction, the Islamobies in the other, while neither is able to consider that there is not the slightest reason why exactly the same should not apply to both sides? Well, collectivism has never been very logical. So when will politicians ban fireworks?

title_en: Social networks are not for minors
text_en:
Bureaucrats in the European Union are preparing a law according to which social networks should be banned for those under thirteen, while young people between the ages of thirteen and sixteen should only be allowed to go there with parental consent; what to say to that? Firstly, perhaps we can all see what rubbish this is, as the state once again declares its intention to raise children instead of parents, and if this continues, in a few generations it will be the norm that raising children is the domain of the state, and if anyone dares to say that parents should do it, they will be branded an extremist; and secondly, I hope that it is also clear to all of us how incredible this piece of shit is, because we can imagine how such a law can be enforced in practice.
There are two possibilities how the whole thing can turn out if the law passes (it hasn't been approved yet): Either there will be some kind of state consent database or similar madness, or the law can be skillfully used as a stick to beat inconvenient dogs - then (in both cases) it will be a mess; or, in practice, it will end up with a parental consent checkbox being added to the checkbox for agreeing to the terms and conditions - then it will be comically toothless and it will be even more experienced that breaking the law is the norm, which would be nice. So we have three options: (a) The law will not pass, (b) the law will pass and someone will actually start enforcing it, or (c) the law will pass and it will be a joke to the rabbits; option (b) is scary, but I find it unlikely, personally I guess (a) is more likely. Reader tips are most welcome in the discussion.

I recently heard Miloš Zeman speak again on the topic of mandatory elections, of which he is a great and long-term supporter. Since only about half of the voters participate in this democratic process, it is not enough for the rulers and they would like more; and when they want something, there is nothing easier than simply ordering people to do it. Here, however, the situation is that only the president really wants it, who in turn lacks the power to enforce it, ergo we will most likely not see mandatory elections in the foreseeable future; however, it is not completely excluded in the future, as there are countries in which citizens have this obligation (if they do not want to participate, they pay a fine).
At first sight, of course, such an idea struck me as monstrous, for such a law is morally unjustifiable; the question is what would be the practical effects? In the first place, it would no doubt incite the people against the authorities, which is always a good thing. Furthermore, in my opinion, a similar law would provide room for more effective mockery of democracy; for example, in Germany there is a political party called "The Party" (in the original "Die PARTEI"), which has only one point in its program: "We will do nothing," for which it understandably does not have much support, but which mandatory voting could change.
Not to mention the fact that something could possibly be gained from compulsory voting by founding a party that will, first of all, promise to abolish compulsory voting; in addition, she could still come up with a libertarian program, ideally smuggled in Trojan style – the official program will only abolish the voting obligation, but in case of potential success she could still liberalize a little in the parliament, or at least use the attention of the media to spread libertarian ideas. The question, of course, is how many of the approximately half of non-voters do not vote simply out of laziness and how many out of some principle, which would greatly influence who these people would be willing to vote for in the event of an election.
So although we can certainly be glad that voting is not compulsory here (less potential buzz), personally I would not be so worried about its introduction, because our situation cannot deteriorate that much (except, of course, another demented state regulation), on the other hand, perhaps such a law could result in some liberalization or at least a weakening of the state in the eyes of its voters and their further annoyance; the question, of course, is to what extent this would affect anything. What do you think about it, dear readers?

So the state finances culture from the pockets of taxpayers in order to take care of it better than terrible private individuals, but apparently it does not understand what every barbaric math physicist Urza does, that is, that part of the work of art is also its name, the change of which changes the artist's message; or is someone seriously going to tell me that if the painting "Hottentot Whore" is renamed "Smoking Woman of the Khoi Tribe" by a callous kokot, the information will not be lost and with it part of the author's statement? Bitcoin probably needs no introduction here; what libertarian wouldn't be excited about a currency that isn't controlled by the state? A huge number of texts have already been written on this topic, the authors of which not only describe Bitcoin, but at the same time venture into various predictions of the future of this virtual currency, with regard to the economic and technical side of the matter; although I share their enthusiasm to a large extent, I also believe that one extremely important factor is often neglected within it - the fucking state. Even if several politicians have not already declared their intention to ban Bitcoin in case it becomes widely used, this step is more than expected from the state - after all, what government will voluntarily give up a monetary monopoly?
Creating a social demand for a ban will be a completely trivial task - it will be enough to find and thoroughly investigate in the media a real or fictitious network of pedophiles trading for bitcoins (it doesn't even have to be true, just fill the media with it); subsequently, a bag of various "experts" will be torn open, confirming that bitcoin is not only the currency of pedophiles, but also of terrorists, thieves and tax evaders. And law enforcement? Well, some will argue that due to decentralization, it is practically impossible to effectively take bitcoins from people, which is true, on the other hand, it is very easy to ban sellers from accepting bitcoins; and anyone who will accept this currency in the online store will complain. Crap? Sure, but who cares but libertarians? Of course, it is right to keep trying to resist, but I fear that Bitcoin will suffer the same fate as Bernard von NotHaus. Does anyone have a more optimistic view? Please share it in the discussion.

title_en: How do we lose our freedom?
text_en:
Some time ago I poured into Stok
comment
, which in turn several people wrote to me that I should insert it as a standard "article"; since in my opinion it is long enough for Stoky, here (a little more generally) I describe its point - how we lose our freedom.
Phase One:
We have some freedom (speech, movement, business, arms, ...); people are not willing to give it up (yet) and anyone who would try to limit this freedom because of some bureaucratic bullshit will be sent somewhere, he will start losing voters and all his colleagues will give up on him. If, by chance, someone just passes a law that cancels this freedom, everyone who promises to repeal this legislation will do better in the next election.
Phase Two:
Prohibitionists present a strong emotional reason to limit this freedom (terrorist attack, mass-raped children, radioactivity, biological weapons, and so on, just about anything that evokes strong feelings, even though it may be only marginally related to the freedom in question); if it is a major intervention in our lives, he promises that it is a temporary change. I assume that we are all familiar with such arguments on the topic that during war one is allowed or does this and that (giving war as an example of moral heights is also laughable). The hysteria will completely overshadow any reasonable debate on the subject, so the ban will pass.
Phase Three:
As soon as people have become accustomed to the fact that the given freedom is already somewhat restricted, the social engineers will come up with a proposal to reduce the number of murders, rapes, robberies, and the like, if this freedom is suppressed a little more; these efforts sometimes fail, but after a while they still succeed (note that once a regulation is in place, it is virtually never repealed). When that happens, that freedom will begin to be restricted without the interest of the public, even because of every fool and bureaucratic whim; although it was a no-brainer at first, it leaves practically everyone (except a few crazy libertarians) cold at this point.
Phase Four:
Processes (within the public and private sectors), services, goods and norms arise, which are based on the fact that the given freedom is somehow limited; these are then used as arguments why that freedom must remain suppressed. Even if the original reason disappears, or turns out to be pointless from the very beginning, it really doesn't matter anymore. No one is interested in this freedom anymore, moreover, "it is clear to everyone" that it must be limited, because otherwise "it wouldn't work" (because of all the processes that count on that limitation).

title_en: Gasoline, alcohol and a weak acid? Only from eighteen!
text_en:
The Ministry of Health changed the law on the protection of public health (yes, we also have such a law, because our bodies belong to the state) so cleverly that in schools, students are not allowed to come into contact with fuels (the health of young car mechanics) or with weak acids or alcohol (be healthy, chemistry students), so even the chemistry olympiads have an impact; the Ministry of Education promised to fix it, but it turned a blind eye, so nothing.
